traits.name: Armor of Greed (3/Day)
traits.value: When Fafnir is hit by attack, he can choose for the attack to miss instead. If the attack is a Critical Hit, he must spend two uses of this trait to cause it to miss. Each time Fafnir uses this ability, creatures have Advantage on attack rolls against him until the end of his next turn.

traits.name: Aura of Avarice
traits.value: Creatures within 1 mile of Fafnir's lair have Disadvantage on saves against spells and effects that compel them to take or steal things, and they feel deeply protective of their own belongings and covetous of the belongings of others.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day, or 4/Day in Lair)
traits.value: If Fafnir fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The dragon makes three attacks using Bite or Constrict in any combination.

actions.name: Bite
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. *Hit:* 15 (**2d8 + 6**) Piercing damage plus 11 (**2d10**) Poison damage.

actions.name: Constrict
actions.value: *Strength Saving Throw:* DC 18 One Huge or smaller creature Fafnir can see within 10 feet of him. *Failure:* 14 (**4d6**) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 16) and the Restrained condition until the Grapple ends. Fafnir can only grapple one creature at a time with this ability.

actions.name: Misfortune Breath (Recharge 4-6)
actions.value: *Wisdom Saving Throw:* DC 17 Each creature in a 60-foot Line. *Failure:* 31 (**7d8**) Poison damage, and the creature has Disadvantage on D20 Tests until the end of Fafnir's next turn. *Success* Half damage only.

fluffInfo.value: *This small man wears hunting leathers and a cowl decorated with antlers, and he holds a glaive made of antlers.*

These shy fairies dress as small fey herdsmen wearing hide armor, hide boots, cloaks, and cowls, all trimmed in fox fur and with a red sash or tunic. They often ride woodland creatures, such as elk, giant weasels, or snowy giant owls.

*The far darrig thrive in forests such as the Arbonesse and Margreve, and they are close allies to the druids in those woodlands. Some believe they also serve in a hidden fey court, somewhere in or near the Green Duchy of Verrayne.*

fluffInfo.name: Hunters and Herders
fluffInfo.value: The far darrig were the hunters, herders, and equerry of the elven nobility. Some still serve in this capacity in planes where the elves rule. Far darrig carry glaives made from fey antlers; each remains enchanted only as long as a far darrig holds it. Their leaders ride on fey elk the color of foxes, with gleaming green eyes. When these elk shed their antlers, the far darrigs' smiths craft the antlers into the glaives wielded by their people.

fluffInfo.name: Hate Arcanists
fluffInfo.value: While not inherently evil, far darrig are hostile to most humanoids and often attack humanoid spellcasters on sight. If they can be persuaded of a spellcaster's or humanoid's good intentions, they make good guides, scouts, and hunters in dangerous forests.

fluffInfo.name: Serve Hags and Worse
fluffInfo.value: They are sometimes found as thralls or scouts serving hags or other evil fey, but they rarely do so willingly.

traits.name: Enchanted Antlers
traits.value: The far darrig's attacks with its Antler Glaive are magical. When the far darrig hits with an Antler Glaive attack, the weapon deals an extra **1d6** force damage (included in the attack).

traits.name: Speak with Beasts
traits.value: The far darrig can communicate with Beasts as if they shared a language.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The far darrig makes two Antler Glaive attacks.

actions.name: Antler Glaive
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. *Hit:* 8 (**1d10 + 3**) piercing damage or slashing damage (the far darrig's choice) plus 3 (**1d6**) force damage. The target must succeed on a DC 13 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

actions.name: Woodland Friends (1/Day)
actions.value: The far darrig magically calls 1d4 elk or giant weasels. The called Beasts arrive in 1d4 rounds, acting as allies of the far darrig and obeying its spoken commands. The Beasts remain for 1 hour, until the far darrig dies, or until the far darrig dismisses them as a bonus action.

bonusActions.name: Nimble Woodsman
bonusActions.value: The far darrig takes the Dash or Disengage action. The far darrig can use this bonus action only if it is in a forest.

entries: **Languages**: telepathy 120 ft. understands all languages but can't speak

traits.name: Fully Contaminated
traits.value: The far dweller is immune to Contamination and has Advantage on saving throws against contaminated spells. The far dweller may cast contaminated spells even though it does not gain Contamination levels.

traits.name: Delerium Healing
traits.value: As an action, the far dweller can touch a delerium shard to regain 10 (3d6) Hit Points. Once the far dweller has used a delerium shard in this way, the shard can't be used in this manner again for 24 hours.

traits.name: Alien Intellect
traits.value: The far dweller is immune to any effect that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts, as well as any divination spell that it refuses. Wisdom (*Insight*) checks made to ascertain the far dweller's intentions or sincerity have Disadvantage.

actions.name: Tentacle
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +7, reach 10 ft. *Hit:* 15 (**2d10 + 4**) Force damage, and the target has the Dazed condition until the end of its next turn.

actions.name: Contaminate
actions.value: *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 16, one creature within 120 feet of the far dweller. *Failure:* 36 (**8d8**) Necrotic damage, and the target gains one Contamination level. *Success* Half damage only.

actions.name: Mind Scramble (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: *Intelligence Saving Throw:* DC 16, each creature in a 60-foot Cone (creatures maintaining *Concentration* have Disadvantage). *Failure:* 28 (**8d6**) Psychic damage, or 48 Psychic damage if the target was maintaining *Concentration*. *Success* Half damage.

bonusActions.name: Pluck the Puppet Strings
bonusActions.value: *Wisdom Saving Throw:* DC 16, one creature within 60 feet of the far dweller. *Failure:* 14 (**4d6**) Psychic damage, and the target must immediately use its Reaction to move up to its Speed toward a creature of the far dweller's choice. If it ends this movement within reach of the creature, it must make a melee weapon attack against the creature with Advantage. *Success* Half damage only.

fluffInfo.name: Study the Foe
fluffInfo.value: Characters proficient in *History* or *Nature* gain Advantage on Intelligence (*Arcana*) checks when they take the Study action to examine a Far Dweller Abductor, learning the following based on the result.

fluffInfo.name: (10+) Psychic Fortress
fluffInfo.value: You learn the creature's Resistances and Immunities.

fluffInfo.name: (15+) Confounding Existence
fluffInfo.value: You are aware of the creature's Unfathomable Presence trait.

fluffInfo.name: (20+) Malign Brilliance
fluffInfo.value: They learn the creature's highest and lowest ability scores.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: The Far Dweller Abductors are not fighters, and simply wish to gather specimens and study them. When Abductors appear, they usually do so when a creature is resting or asleep. They rely on their Unfathomable Presence to confuse and dismantle their target. They use use Mind Warp or Devour Thoughts to weaken the mind of their target before attempting to Abduct them.

The Far Dweller Abductors do not wish to be observed or remembered, and do not want even their dead left behind to be discovered and known to the creatures they are researching. A Far Dweller Abductor will teleport away and use __Plane Shift__ if it has lost the upper hand, is outnumbered, or feels in any way threatened. If a Far Dweller Abductor dies, any Far Dwellers still engaged in battle attempt to take their bodies and vanish as quickly as possible, attempting to leave no trace of their presence.

fluffInfo.name: Animus:
fluffInfo.value: Aberration.

fluffInfo.name: Fluid:
fluffInfo.value: Contaminated Ichor, Mucus.

fluffInfo.name: Organs:
fluffInfo.value: Heart, Brain, Guts.

fluffInfo.name: Bones:
fluffInfo.value: Spine.

fluffInfo.name: Natural Weapons:
fluffInfo.value: Tentacles.

fluffInfo.name: Hide:
fluffInfo.value: Skin.

fluffInfo.name: Dust:
fluffInfo.value: Aberrant Dust.

entries: **Languages**: telepathy 120 ft. understands all languages but can't speak

traits.name: Fully Contaminated
traits.value: The far dweller is immune to Contamination and has Advantage on saving throws against contaminated spells. The far dweller may cast contaminated spells even though it does not gain Contamination levels.

traits.name: Delerium Healing
traits.value: As an action, the far dweller can touch a delerium shard to regain 10 (3d6) Hit Points. Once the far dweller has used a delerium shard in this way, the shard can't be used in this manner again for 24 hours.

traits.name: Alien Intellect
traits.value: The far dweller is immune to any effect that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts, as well as any divination spell that it refuses. Wisdom (*Insight*) checks made to ascertain the far dweller's intentions or sincerity have Disadvantage.

traits.name: Unfathomable Presence
traits.value: A creature that starts its turn within 120 feet of the far dweller and can see it is subjected to the following effect. *Intelligence Saving Throw:* DC 15. *Failure:* The target has the Blinded and Immobilized conditions until the start of its next turn. *Success* The target is immune to the Unfathomable Presence of all far dweller abductors for 24 hours.

Unless *surprised*, a creature can avert its eyes to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If the creature does so, it has Disadvantage on attack rolls against the far dweller until the start of its next turn. If the creature looks at the far dweller in the meantime, that creature must immediately make the saving throw.

actions.name: Mind Warp
actions.value: *Ranged Attack Roll:* +7, range 120 ft. *Hit:* 27 (**4d10 + 5**) Psychic damage, and the target must roll 1d4 and subtract the result from the next saving throw it makes before the end of the far dweller's next turn.

actions.name: Devour Thoughts
actions.value: *Intelligence Saving Throw:* DC 15, one creature within 30 feet of the far dweller. *Failure:* 19 (**4d6 + 5**) Psychic damage, and the target's Intelligence score is reduced by 1d4. If this effect reduces the target's Intelligence to 0, it has the Paralyzed condition. The reduction lasts until the target finishes a Short or Long Rest.

actions.name: Abduct
actions.value: The far dweller casts __Plane Shift__ without components, targeting itself and each Incapacitated creature within 10 feet of it.

bonusActions.name: Psychic Step
bonusActions.value: The far dweller magically teleports to an unoccupied space it can see within 60 feet.

entries: **Languages**: telepathy 120 ft. Understand all languages but can't speak

traits.name: Fully Contaminated
traits.value: The far dweller is immune to Contamination and has Advantage on saving throws against contaminated spells. The far dweller may cast contaminated spells even though it does not gain Contamination levels.

traits.name: Delerium Healing

traits.name: Eldritch Aura
traits.value: A creature that starts its turn within 30 feet of the far dweller takes 10 (**3d6**) Psychic damage.

traits.name: Magic Deflection
traits.value: The far dweller has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects. If the far dweller is targeted by a spell of level 4 or lower, the caster must succeed on a DC 19 Intelligence saving throw or the spell fails and the caster takes 18 (**4d8**) Psychic damage.

actions.name: The far dweller always takes its turn on Initiative count 20
actions.value: On its turn, the far dweller can use its movement and interaction as normal. However, it does not take an action or Bonus Action on its turn unless forced to do so by a spell or other effect. Instead, the far dweller takes one of the following Epic Actions at the end of each player character's turn:

entries: **Tentacle**: *Melee Attack Roll:* +11, reach 10 ft. *Hit:* 22 (**3d10 + 6**) Force damage, and the target has the Dazed condition until the end of its next turn.

**Contaminate**: *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 19, one creature within 120 feet of the far dweller. *Failure:* 45 (**10d8**) Necrotic damage, and the target gains one Contamination level. *Success* Half damage only.

actions.name: Mind Scramble (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: *Intelligence Saving Throw:* DC 19, each creature in a 60-foot Cone (creatures maintaining *Concentration* have Disadvantage). *Failure:* 42 (**12d6**) Psychic damage, or 72 Psychic damage if the target was maintaining *Concentration*. *Success* Half damage.

actions.name: Pluck the Puppet Strings (1/Round)
actions.value: *Wisdom Saving Throw:* DC 19, one creature within 120 feet of the far dweller. *Failure:* 28 (**8d6**) Psychic damage, and the target must immediately use its Reaction to move up to its Speed toward a creature of the far dweller's choice. If it ends this movement within reach of the creature, it must make a melee weapon attack against the creature with Advantage. *Success* Half damage only.

actions.name: Phase Out (1/Round)
actions.value: The far dweller teleports to an unoccupied space within 120 feet of it. Each creature within 10 feet of the far dweller when it arrives is subjected to the following effect. *Intelligence Saving Throw:* DC 19. *Failure:* 21 (**6d6**) Psychic damage, and the target has the Defenseless condition until the end of its next turn. *Success* Half damage only.

actions.name: Epic Resistance
actions.value: The far dweller chooses one condition, spell, or other effect currently affecting them and rolls 1d20. On an 11+, the effect ends on it. The far dweller can use this action even if it would otherwise be unable to take actions, its actions are being controlled by another creature, or if a spell or effect alters its game statistics.

fluffInfo.value: *Violet radiance surrounds this large pale centipede. Its flesh is translucent, and its jaws are crystalline.*

fluffInfo.name: Destiny Destroyers
fluffInfo.value: Fate eaters infest remote areas of the planes, where they consume the threads of Fate itself. The beings in charge of Fate view them as vermin. Sometimes those beings engage particularly canny planar travelers either to hunt fate eaters or to help repair the damage they've done. This can be a deadly job, as the fate eaters consider the destiny of a mortal to be the tastiest of delicacies, rich in savory possibilities.

fluffInfo.name: Planar Gossips
fluffInfo.value: Fate eaters can and do trade information about various dooms, fates, and outcomes, but one must have something rich in destiny to trade—or at least, juicy gossip about gods and demons.

fluffInfo.name: Visionary Flesh
fluffInfo.value: Eating the properly prepared flesh of a fate eater grants the eater insight into the fate of another being.

entries: **Languages**: telepathy 100 ft. understands all but can't speak

traits.name: Visionary Flesh
traits.value: A creature that eats the flesh of a fate eater must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the creature is poisoned for 1 hour. On a success, the creature gains the benefits of the divination spell.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The fate eater makes two Bite attacks.

actions.name: Bite
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 13 (**2d8 + 4**) slashing damage plus 7 (**2d6**) necrotic damage.

actions.name: Alter Fate (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: The fate eater alters the fate of one creature it can see within 30 feet of it. The creature must make a DC 15 Charisma saving throw. On a failure, the creature takes 36 (**8d8**) psychic damage, and its fate is altered. Roll a d6 to determine which of the following alterations affects the creature. On a success, the creature takes half the damage, and its fate isn't altered. A creature with an altered fate for 1 minute or less can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. Otherwise, a creature with an altered fate can repeat the saving throw at the end of each long rest, ending the effect on itself on a success.

actions.name: 1 Forgotten Training
actions.value: The creatures loses the use of one random class feature, such as Action Surge or Channel Divinity, for 1 minute.

actions.name: 2 Lost Potential
actions.value: One of the creature's ability scores, chosen at random, is reduced by 2.

actions.name: 3 Seeing the Alternates
actions.value: The creature is incapacitated for 1 minute.

actions.name: 4 Shifting Memories
actions.value: The creature loses proficiency in one random skill and gains proficiency in another random skill.

actions.name: 5 Took the Lesser Path
actions.value: The creature's current hp total becomes its hp maximum.

actions.name: 6 Untied from the Loop
actions.value: When the creature moves, it moves in a random direction for 1 minute.

traits.name: Eldritch Mind
traits.value: The warlock has advantage on saving throws made to maintain its concentration.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The warlock makes three simultaneous Eldritch Blast attacks against the same or different targets within range.

actions.name: Dagger
actions.value: *Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack:* +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. *Hit:* 5 (**1d4 + 3**) piercing damage.

actions.name: Eldritch Blast
actions.value: Ranged Spell Attack: +9 to hit, range 300 ft., one creature. *Hit:* 10 (**1d10 + 5**) force damage and the warlock can choose to move the target 10 feet further from or closer to the warlock in a straight line.

actions.name: Plunge of the Deep (1/Short or Long Rest)
actions.value: The warlock teleports it and up to six other willing creatures it can see within 30 feet of it to a body of water it has seen (pond-sized or larger) within 2 miles of it.

bonusActions.name: Fathomcaller's Tentacle (4/Day)
bonusActions.value: The warlock summons a 10-foot-long tentacle at a point it can see within 60 feet of it, which lasts for 1 minute or until it uses this action again. When it creates the tentacle, the warlock can make a melee spell attack (+9 to hit) with the tentacle against a target within 10 feet of it, dealing 9 (**2d8**) cold damage on a hit. On its subsequent turns, the warlock can use a bonus action to move the tentacle up to 30 feet and repeat the attack.

fluffInfo.value: *This well-dressed figure appears elven, save for its featureless face and taloned hands.*

Known as a fiarsídhe among themselves, fear smiths are servants of shadow fey courts and other, similar dark fey courts. While its mouth is closed, a fear smith's face is featureless save for rows of deep wrinkles. Opening the large mouth in the center of its face reveals long needlelike teeth surrounding a single, massive eye.

fluffInfo.name: Icy-Cold Eyes
fluffInfo.value: Fear smiths often serve as torturers or are dispatched to demoralize the court's enemies. Their stare stops enemies cold, making it easy for heavily-armed warriors to trap and finish a foe.

fluffInfo.name: Devour Fear
fluffInfo.value: Fear smiths feed off strong emotions, and their favorite meal is terror. The fey prefer prolonging the death of victims, and, when free to indulge, a fear smith stalks its victim for days before attacking, hinting at its presence to build dread.

fluffInfo.name: Hoods and Masks
fluffInfo.value: Fear smiths favor fine clothing and high fashion, donning hooded cloaks or masks when discretion is required. Eerily well-mannered and respectful, fear smiths enjoy feigning civility and playing the part of nobility, speaking genteelly but with a thick, unidentifiable accent.

entries: **Resistances**: bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from attacks not made with cold iron weapons

traits.name: Distortion Gaze
traits.value: Those who meet the gaze of the fear smith experience the world seeming to twist at unnatural angles beneath their feet. When a creature that can see the fear smith's eye starts its turn within 30 feet of the fear smith, the fear smith can force the creature to make a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw if the fear smith isn't incapacitated and can see the creature. On a failed save, the creature is disoriented until the start of its next turn. While disoriented, a creature can't take the Dash or Disengage action, and when it moves for the first time on its turn, it must succeed on a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw or fall prone.

Unless surprised, a creature can avert its eyes to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If the creature does so, it can't see the fear smith until the start of its next turn, when it can avert its eyes again. If the creature looks at the fear smith in the meantime, it must immediately make the save.

traits.name: Hidden Eye
traits.value: The fear smith has advantage on saving throws against being blinded.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.value: The fear smith has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The fear smith makes three Claw attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Heart-Stopping Stare.

actions.name: Claw
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 12 (**2d8 + 3**) slashing damage plus 9 (**2d8**) psychic damage. If the target is disoriented by Distortion Gaze, the fear smith regains hp equal to the amount of psychic damage dealt.

actions.name: Heart-Stopping Stare
actions.value: The fear smith terrifies a creature within 30 feet of it with a look. The target must succeed on a DC 16 Wisdom saving throw or take 13 (**3d8**) psychic damage and be stunned until the end of its next turn. The fear smith regains hp equal to the psychic damage dealt.

fluffInfo.value: Fell wraiths appear as crooked wanderers, roaming among ancient ruins, wrapped in cloaks hiding their spectral features. Their flesh is almost transparent, and their eyes seem to glow like embers. If encountered in the hours of twilight, they may pass as Men, as they can speak, even if with an unusual hissing voice and strange accents. Fell Wraiths carry old weapons, relics from an age of strife that they employ to deadly effectiveness.

entries: **Resistances**: bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from weapons that aren't enchanted with spells for the Bane of the undead
**Immunities**: cold, necrotic, poison; charmed, exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained

traits.name: Deathless
traits.value: If damage reduces the Fell Wraith to 0 hit points, it must make a Constitution saving throw with a DC of 5 + the damage taken, unless the damage is radiant, from a critical hit, or from a weapon enchanted with spells for the Bane of the Undead. On a success, the Fell Wraith drops to 1 hit point instead.

traits.name: Sunlight Weakness
traits.value: While in sunlight, the Fell Wraith has disadvantage on attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The Fell Wraith can use its Strike Fear. It then makes a melee attack.

actions.name: Sword
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 6 (**1d6 + 3**) slashing damage, or 7 (**1d8 + 3**) slashing damage if used with two hands to make a melee attack.

actions.name: Strike Fear
actions.value: Each non-undead creature of the Fell Wraith's choice that is within 60 feet of the Fell Wraith and aware of it gains 1 Shadow point from Dread, resisted by a DC 12 Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, a target becomes frightened for 1 minute. If the save fails by 5 or more, the target is also stunned while frightened in this way. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If a creature's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is immune to the Fell Wraith's Strike Fear for the next 24 hours.

fluffInfo.value: *A darkly foreboding intelligence glows behind this automaton's eyes, and its joints seep hissing green vapors.*

*Dwarves of Grisal canton create fellforged to fight against undead haunts and spirits and melt them down afterwards, destroying wraiths, ghosts, and other incorporeal undead. The fellforged are also sometimes created by the Emerald Order and other cults seeking to give their evil masters a body and a shape with which to rule.*

fluffInfo.name: Spectral Constructs
fluffInfo.value: Fellforged are the castoffs of gearforged and clockworks production, given foul sentience when the construct bodies attract specters yearning to feel the corporeal world. The clockwork bodies trap the specters, but it gives them physical form. The specters twist the bodies to their own use, sometimes going so far as to destroy the body to harm the living. On rare occasions, other ghostly undead choose to inhabit such constructs, using the constructs as tools to enact their will in the living world at the cost of many of their natural abilities and defenses.

fluffInfo.name: Soldiers for Vampires
fluffInfo.value: Fellforged often seek out greater undead as their masters. Vampires and liches are favorite leaders, but mummies and darakhul also make suitable commanders.

fluffInfo.name: Grave Speech
fluffInfo.value: The fellforged's voice is echoing and sepulchral, unnerving most living creatures.

entries: **Immunities**: necrotic, poison, psychic; charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned
**Languages**: the languages it knew in life

traits.name: Construct Nature
traits.value: The fellforged doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

traits.name: Inhabiting Spirit
traits.value: The fellforged is inhabited and animated by a specter. If the fellforged fails a saving throw against an effect that turns undead, the specter is expelled into an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the fellforged with the hp total it had before it was expelled. The specter otherwise uses the statistics of a specter.

Without its animating specter, the fellforged becomes dormant for 1 minute then crumbles to pieces and is destroyed. The expelled specter can reinhabit the dormant fellforged as a bonus action while within 5 feet of the fellforged, making it active again and using the specter's current hp as the fellforged's hp total.

traits.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
traits.value: While in sunlight, the fellforged has disadvantage on attack rolls, as well as on Wisdom (*Perception*) checks that rely on sight.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The fellforged makes two Necrotic Slam attacks.

actions.name: Necrotic Slam
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 9 (**2d6 + 2**) bludgeoning damage plus 9 (**2d8**) necrotic damage. If the target is a creature, it must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or its hp maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the necrotic damage taken. This reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest. The target dies if this effect reduces its hp maximum to 0.

bonusActions.name: Burst Gears
bonusActions.value: The specter within the fellforged strains the construct's body, sending broken springs and gears flying. Each creature within 5 feet of the fellforged must make a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw, taking 7 (**2d6**) piercing damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Each time the fellforged uses this bonus action, its speed is reduced by 5 feet, and it can't use this bonus action if its speed is 0. Its speed returns to normal when it finishes a long rest.

entries: **Languages**: Understands Abyssal and Giant but can't speak

traits.name: Mystical Chain
traits.value: The mystical chain attached to the fenrikyn is its greatest weakness and can be severed by an attack dealing 20 Slashing damage against AC 17, which deals no damage to the fenrikyn. If the fenrikyn's chain is destroyed, it takes 18 (**4d8**) Psychic damage and has the Stunned condition until the end of its next turn. It also loses its Chain Attack action, Whirling Chain action, and Deflecting Chain Reaction.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The fenrikyn makes one Bite attack and one Chain attack. If its Mystical Chain has been broken, it instead makes two Bite attacks.

actions.name: Bite
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 14 (**2d8 + 5**) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Chain
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +8 to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. *Hit:* 12 (**2d6 + 5**) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 16). While grappled, the target cannot move further than 20 feet from the fenrikyn, and its Speed is reduced by 10 feet.

actions.name: Whirling Chain (Recharge 6)
actions.value: *Dexterity Saving Throw:* DC 16 All creatures within 20 feet of the fenrikyn. *Failure:* 21 (**6d6**) Bludgeoning damage, and the target is pushed or pulled 10 feet. *Success* Half damage only.

entries: **Immunities**: fire, poison; charmed, deafened, frightened, paralyzed, poisoned

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (6/Day)
traits.value: If the tarrasque fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.value: The tarrasque has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Reflective Carapace
traits.value: If the tarrasque is targeted by a __Magic Missile__ spell or a spell that requires a ranged attack roll, roll 1d6. On a 1-5, the tarrasque is unaffected. On a 6, the tarrasque is unaffected and reflects the spell, turning the caster into the target.

traits.name: Siege Monster
traits.value: The tarrasque deals double damage to objects and structures.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The tarrasque makes one Bite attack and three other attacks, using Claw or Tail in any combination.

actions.name: Bite
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +19, reach 15 ft. *Hit:* 36 (**4d12 + 10**) Piercing damage, and the target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 20). Until the grapple ends, the target has the Restrained condition and can't teleport.

actions.name: Claw
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +19, reach 15 ft. *Hit:* 28 (**4d8 + 10**) Slashing damage.

actions.name: Tail
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +19, reach 30 ft. *Hit:* 23 (**3d8 + 10**) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Huge or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

actions.name: Thunderous Bellow (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 27, each creature and each object that isn't being worn or carried in a 150-foot Cone. *Failure:* 78 (**12d12**) Thunder damage, and the target has the Deafened and Frightened conditions until the end of its next turn. *Success* Half damage only.

bonusActions.name: Swallow
bonusActions.value: *Strength Saving Throw:* DC 27, one Large or smaller creature Grappled by the tarrasque (it can have up to six creatures swallowed at a time). *Failure:* The target is swallowed, and the Grappled condition ends. A swallowed creature has the Blinded and Restrained conditions and can't teleport, it has Total Cover against attacks and other effects outside the tarrasque, and it takes 56 (**16d6**) Acid damage at the start of each of the tarrasque's turns.

If the tarrasque takes 60 damage or more on a single turn from a creature inside it, the tarrasque must succeed on a DC 20 Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate all swallowed creatures, each of which falls in a space within 10 feet of the tarrasque and has the Prone condition. If the tarrasque dies, any swallowed creature no longer has the Restrained condition and can escape from the corpse using 20 feet of movement, exiting Prone.

fluffInfo.value: *Cursed Undead Boatman*

fluffInfo.name: Secret
fluffInfo.value: Paying a ferryman 3 copper coins lifts any curse the creature placed on the payer, and it entitles one to a single unnerving but safe ride in the ferryman's coffin boat.

entries: **Immunities**: poison; charmed, exhaustion, frightened, poisoned, prone (with Coffin Boat)

traits.name: Coffin Boat
traits.value: The ferryman rides an open coffin on a swell of swamp water, allowing it to travel with a Speed of 40 feet over any surface, including liquids, ignoring Difficult Terrain. The coffin can hold two other Medium creatures. Two Small creatures or four Tiny creatures count as one Medium creature.

While riding the coffin, the ferryman has Immunity to the Prone condition, and the coffin moves with the ferryman unless the ferryman has the Incapacitated condition. The coffin has AC 15; HP 25; Immunity to Necrotic, Poison, and Psychic damage.
If the coffin is destroyed, the ferryman can magically create a new one using a 10-minute ritual.

traits.name: Payment
traits.value: The ferryman must peacefully offer a ride in its boat to a creature that takes the Influence action to offer it 3 CP. If that creature is cursed by the ferryman, the curse ends. If the boat is full, the ferryman must return to offer the creature a ride once its current passengers leave the boat. If the creature or its allies damage the ferryman or force it to make a saving throw, this effect ends and the creature can't use that ferryman's Payment trait again.

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.value: The ferryman regains 10 Hit Points at the start of each of its turns if it has at least 1 Hit Point.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The ferryman makes two Lantern Pole attacks and uses Hexed Lantern if available.

actions.name: Lantern Pole
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +7, reach 10 ft. *Hit:* 9 (**1d10 + 4**) Bludgeoning damage plus 7 (**2d6**) Necrotic damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Prone condition.

actions.name: Hexed Lantern (1/Day)
actions.value: *Wisdom Saving Throw:* DC 13, each creature of the ferryman's choice in a 30-foot Cone. *Failure:* The creature is cursed for 1 minute and must subtract 1d4 from D20 Tests.

fluffInfo.value: *Fungal Undead Giant*

fluffInfo.name: Secret
fluffInfo.value: Festerhulks shrink from sunlight, which harms the fungus that animates them.

entries: **Immunities**: necrotic, poison; exhaustion, poisoned, stunned, unconscious
**Languages**: understands Common and Giant but can't speak

traits.name: Fungal Step
traits.value: The festerhulk ignores Difficult Terrain caused by plants or fungi.

traits.name: Spore Cloud
traits.value: At the end of each of the festerhulk's turns, each creature in a 5-foot Emanation originating from the festerhulk takes 10 (**3d6**) Necrotic damage and has the Poisoned condition until the end of its next turn. A Giant or Humanoid killed by this damage rises as a new creature 24 hours later: Festerhulk (if a Giant), __Zombie__ (if a Humanoid).

traits.name: Sunlight Hypersensitivity
traits.value: The festerhulk takes 10 Radiant damage if it starts its turn in sunlight. While in sunlight, it has Disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks.

actions.name: Multiattack

actions.name: Fetid Slam

actions.name: Slime Mold (1/Day)
actions.value: The festerhulk disgorges a mass of ravenous slime mold into an unoccupied space within 20 feet. This mass uses the Black Pudding stat block except it is a Plant, and its size is Medium. The mass acts on the festerhulk's Initiative. It, and any masses it Split into, dries up and dies in 1 hour.

traits.name: Divine Strike (1/Turn)
traits.value: When the battlechef hits a creature with a weapon attack, the battlechef can cause the attack to deal an extra 4 (**1d8**) acid or poison damage (battlechef's choice) to the target.

traits.name: Poison Resilience
traits.value: The battlechef has advantage on saving throws against poisoned.

traits.name: Strong Stomach (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
traits.value: While the battlechef is drunkenness, it can choose to magically suppress the alcohol's effects for 1 minute.

actions.name: Handaxe
actions.value: *Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack:* +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. *Hit:* 6 (**1d6 + 3**) slashing damage.

actions.name: Create Healing Draft (Recharges after a Short or Long Rest)
actions.value: The battlechef creates a magical potion in its free hand or at its feet (battlechef's choice). A creature that drinks this potion regains 15 (2d6 + 8) hit points. The potion turns to dust and is lost if the battlechef finishes a short or long rest before it is consumed.

fluffInfo.value: *Taut dead skin, adorned entirely with tattooed fish scales, covers this woman's face and hands. She wears scaled armor, sea green like verdigris on copper, and wields a sword swirling with arcane energies. Her pale eyes stare, unblinking*.

fluffInfo.name: Undead Warlock Vassals
fluffInfo.value: Ancient and powerful beings across the multiverse grant magical knowledge to mortals through dangerous pacts. Those bound to these pacts become warlocks, but the will and force of their patron is borne by more than just those who strike bargains for sorcerous power. A fext is a former warlock who has become wholly dedicated to their patron—mind, body, and soul—and functions as enforcer, bodyguard, and assassin. They are powerful undead slaves to the will of their otherworldly patron.

fluffInfo.name: Linked to a Master
fluffInfo.value: Each fext is a unique servant of their patron and exhibits the physical traits of its master. The eyes of every fext are tied directly to their patron's mind, who can see what the fext sees at any time. The fext also possesses a telepathic link to its patron. The process a warlock undergoes to become a fext is horrendous. The warlock is emptied of whatever morality and humanity he or she had as wine from a jug, and the patron imbues the empty vessel with its corruption and unearthly will. Whatever life the fext led before is completely gone. They exist only to serve.

fluffInfo.name: Outdoing Rivals
fluffInfo.value: Scholars have debated about how many fext a patron can command. The more powerful and well-established have at least 100, while others have only a handful. Where there is more than one fext, however, they maneuver amongst themselves to curry favor with their powerful patron. Each fext is bound to obey commands, but they attempt to carry out the commands to the detriment of their competitors. Scheming is common and rampant among them, and each fext tries to work without the aid of other fext as much as possible.

entries: **Resistances**: bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from nonmagical attacks
**Immunities**: poison; charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, poisoned
**Languages**: the languages it knew in life

traits.name: Eldritch Weapons
traits.value: The fext's weapon attacks are magical. When the fext hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra **2d8** force damage (included in the attack).

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.value: The fext has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Patron's Blessing
traits.value: While the fext is conscious and wearing no armor and wielding no shield, it adds its Charisma modifier to its AC (included above).

traits.name: Undead Nature
traits.value: The fext doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The fext makes two Eldritch Blade or Eldritch Fury attacks.

actions.name: Eldritch Blade
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 12 (**2d8 + 3**) slashing damage plus 9 (**2d8**) force damage.

actions.name: Eldritch Fury
actions.value: *Ranged Spell Attack:* +7 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. *Hit:* 17 (**3d8 + 4**) force damage.

actions.name: Patron's Might (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: The fext channels its patron's awe‑inspiring presence, terrifying those nearby. Each creature within 10 feet of the fext must make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, a creature takes 35 (**10d6**) psychic damage and is frightened for 1 minute. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn't frightened. A frightened creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

fluffInfo.value: *Dark, bark-like rust encrusts the trunk of this metal tree, and its dull metallic leaves rustle with the sound of sharp metal.*

fluffInfo.name: Cold Iron Trees
fluffInfo.value: These ferrous constructs are cold-forged in a process taking several years, as bits of rust and other oxidation are cultivated one layer at a time into bark and branches. In this way, the artificers create massive, twisted trunks resembling real, gnarled trees. Green-tinged leaves of beaten cold iron are welded in place by the master craftsmen, and trained warmages bring the construct to life through intense magical rituals rumored to take a full turn of seasons.

fluffInfo.name: Fey Destroyers
fluffInfo.value: The feyward tree unswervingly obeys the commands of its creators, guarding key points of entry across fey rivers and streams, abandoned sacred groves deep in the forest, suspected faerie rings, or possible elf encampments. Many are released deep in elvish woods with orders to attack any fey on sight. These trees are rarely, if ever, heard from again. Whether they leave a bloody trail of flayed elves in their wake or some fey counter-measure neutralizes them is unknown.

fluffInfo.name: Growing Numbers
fluffInfo.value: Each year, the feywardens order the construction and release of a handful of feyward trees, trusting in the destructive nature of the constructs. The feywardens leave nothing to chance, flooding fey forests with the constructs over decades.

fluffInfo.value: *What appears to be a mated pair of birds changes into two bestial celestials that move in perfect harmony.*
Fidele angels form from souls so devoted to each other that their love transcends death.

fluffInfo.name: Friends to Lovers
fluffInfo.value: Fideles are charged with exhorting mortals to respect the bonds of partnership. They assist lovers facing obstacles and punish the enemies of love. Where there is a conflict between two cultures' laws in love, they prefer the result that keeps lovers together.

fluffInfo.name: Quiet Diplomats
fluffInfo.value: They prefer diplomacy to force and, despite the urgency of love, they've been known to live secretly among mortals for years or decades while waging quiet campaigns against social mores and cultural norms that keep love from achieving its full potential.

The angel that was the original target of the attack takes any damage that won't divide evenly. All other effects, such as reducing ability scores or being the target of a __bless__ spell, affect only the target.

actions.name: To My Lover's Side
actions.value: If its mate is more than 1 mile away from it, the fidele angel can magically teleport, along with any equipment it is wearing or carrying, to an unoccupied space within 10 feet of its mate. The angel can use this action even if its mate is on another plane of existence.

bonusActions.name: Change Shape
bonusActions.value: The fidele angel transforms into a Medium or smaller Humanoid, a Large or smaller birdlike Beast, or back into its true form, which is a winged Celestial. Without wings, it loses its flying speed. Its statistics, other than its size and speed, are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed. It reverts to its true form if it dies.

actions.name: Brittlebone Splinterspray Tommybow

fluffInfo.value: A Soulbound Host is the physical body of an apothecary who has willingly allowed an extraplanar creature to possess them, trapping the powerful outsider in a mortal form. Powerful yet vulnerable, Soulbound Hosts loathe their creators. They wander the world for the means to reverse the curse of mortality placed upon them and return to their otherworldly domains.

Exorcist and Alienist apothecaries do not primarily study the body, and rarely practice the type of magic and science which leads to mutant horrors and flesh-stitched abominations. They are instead concerned with the supernatural forces of the mind and soul. Many research and contact powerful extraplanar entities, eager to possess mortals as a means of entering the material world. These apothecaries learn how to create Soulbound Hosts as a powerful means to contain and fight back against these dangerous otherworldly foes.

fluffInfo.name: Desperate Gambit
fluffInfo.value: A Soulbound Host is usually created under truly desperate circumstances, such as when a heroic apothecary faces a dangerous otherworldly being such as a demon, fey, spirit, or inscrutable entity from the Space Between Worlds. Not only are these planar invaders pernicious foes, many are effectively immortal—often these creatures simply reform when killed outside their native planes. Thus, an apothecary who lacks the ability to defeat the demon on their own, or who wishes to defeat a powerful outsider in a more permanent fashion, may instead decide upon a heroic act of self-sacrifice by turning themselves into a Soulbound Host.

fluffInfo.name: Preparing the Trap
fluffInfo.value: Using an array of implanted metals, ingested tinctures, mental preparations, and occult incantations, a skilled apothecary may willingly prepare their body for possession. During the process, the apothecary can weave a unique spiritual trap. It then falls to the apothecary to convince the otherworldly creature to possess them, an act that many outsiders are eager to do. Thus, the canny apothecary preys on the ego of the monster itself.

fluffInfo.name: Mortal Curse
fluffInfo.value: When the outsider inhabits the body, the apothecary's soul departs, leaving the extraplanar creature to take their place spiritually. If this mortal form is killed or destroyed, the bound creature does not simply return to their plane of origin. Instead, the spirit departs to the afterworlds like any other mortal soul, losing their accumulated otherworldly power forever. Thus, the Soulbound Host becomes both a prison and a death sentence for the other wielding being tricked into the apothecary's body.

fluffInfo.name: Rogue Hosts
fluffInfo.value: Unfortunately, this act of self-sacrifice is not without its imperfections. The apothecary's body is filled with otherworldly essence, and while the creature's power is greatly diminished, they often remain extremely dangerous—allies of the departed apothecary may still find it challenging to slay the Soulbound Host. Many escape, wandering the world with stolen lives and even assuming the identity of their host while they search for the means to escape their now mortal form. All bound outsiders are painfully aware of their new mortality, frustrated that returning to their planes of origin is not a simple matter of destroying their flesh-cage or switching their essence into a different host, one which lacks the binding wards placed by the apothecary.

fluffInfo.name: Price of Freedom
fluffInfo.value: Trapped outsiders can win their freedom by calling back the soul of the apothecary who trapped them, and resurrecting them into their body. This is a thing many outsiders are loathe to do out of fiendish ego, since it puts the original soul in a bargaining position. In this way, the apothecary can force the spirit to accept a bargain which requires them to remain in their own worlds for at least the duration of the apothecary's lifetime.

fluffInfo.name: Study the Foe
fluffInfo.value: Characters proficient in *Religion*, *Medicine*, or *Survival* gain Advantage on Wisdom (*Insight*) or Intelligence (*Investigation*) checks to Study a Soulbound Host, learning the following based on the result:

fluffInfo.name: (10+) Possessed Body
fluffInfo.value: You know the Soulbound Host's type and damage Resistances.

fluffInfo.name: (15+) Extraplanar Magic
fluffInfo.value: Depending on the type of spirit, you learn either the Hellfire Chain, Illusory Assault, or Psychic Barrage actions, as well as the Spellcasting trait of the host.

fluffInfo.name: (20+) Cursed Fate
fluffInfo.value: You recognize its desperation caused by its spirit-bound mortality and its Reactions.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: A Soulbound Host is a careful combatant. Though powerful, the last thing they want is to be killed in their mortal form. If they are seriously injured, they often attempt to bargain, offering power and knowledge to assailants who spare them.

traits.value: The elemental can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing. A creature that touches the elemental or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it takes 5 (**1d10**) fire damage. In addition, the elemental can enter a hostile creature's space and stop there. The first time it enters a creature's space on a turn, that creature takes 5 (**1d10**) fire damage and catches fire; until someone takes an action to douse the fire, the creature takes 5 (**1d10**) fire damage at the start of each of its turns.

fluffInfo.value: *This proud bird struts like a peacock, made all the more majestic by its flaming fan of feathers, which shift through the color spectrum.*

fluffInfo.name: Guides and Helpers
fluffInfo.value: Firebirds are welcome sights to those in need of warmth and safety. They primarily work at night or in underground areas, where their talents are most needed. Friendly to all creatures, they become aggressive only upon witnessing obviously evil acts. Firebirds enjoy working with good adventuring parties, providing light and healing, though their wanderlust prevents them from staying for long.

fluffInfo.name: Redeemers
fluffInfo.value: Firebirds enjoy acting as reformers. They search for creatures they perceive as potential "light bringers," and they grant boons to such creatures, magically coaxing the creatures into performing good deeds in the hope such acts redeem the creatures.

fluffInfo.name: Magical Feathers
fluffInfo.value: Firebird feathers are prized throughout the mortal world, and occasionally, the creatures bestow feathers upon those they favor. Firebirds also seed hidden locations with specialized feathers, which burst into full-grown firebirds after a year. Firebirds live over 100 years.

entries: **Resistances**: bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from nonmagical attacks

traits.name: Enforce Good Deeds
traits.value: A creature that has received assistance, such as healing or a glowing feather, from the firebird must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or be affected by the __geas__ spell for 30 days. While under the geas, the affected creature must assist nonhostile creatures suffering from starvation or thirst by alleviating the starvation or thirst.

traits.name: Fiery Weapons
traits.value: The firebird's weapon attacks are magical. When the firebird hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra **2d6** fire damage (included in the attack).

traits.name: Glowing Feathers
traits.value: The firebird sheds bright light in a 5- to 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional number of feet equal to the chosen radius. The firebird can alter the radius as a bonus action. If the firebird willingly gifts a feather to a creature, the feather sheds bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 feet indefinitely.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.value: The firebird has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Warming Presence
traits.value: The firebird and each creature within 5 feet of it are immune to the effects of cold environments, provided the cold is caused by naturally occurring weather and climate. When the firebird is inside a structure, it can choose for this trait to affect all creatures within the structure (no action required), regardless of how close they are to it.

actions.value: The firebird makes one Beak attack and one Talon attack.

actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 7 (**1d6 + 4**) piercing damage plus 7 (**2d6**) fire damage.

actions.name: Talon

On a failure, a creature takes 17 (**5d6**) fire damage and is blinded until the end of its next turn. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn't blinded.

actions.name: Healing Feathers (3/Day)
actions.value: The firebird touches another creature, brushing its wings against the creature. The target magically regains 10 3d6 hp and is freed from any disease, poison, blindness, or deafness.

fluffInfo.value: *Wisps of black smoke and spots of bright flame coalesce into a vaguely humanoid shape.*

fluffInfo.name: Elemental Echoes
fluffInfo.value: When a fire elemental meets its destruction in a particularly humiliating fashion, particularly by humanoids, while summoned away from its home plane, its remains transform into a firegeist. Malevolent and resentful, they exist for revenge.

fluffInfo.name: Indiscriminate Arsonists
fluffInfo.value: Firegeists are not adept at telling one humanoid from another, and they are satisfied with burning any similar creature, providing the creature is flammable.

fluffInfo.name: Brighter Light, Darker Smoke
fluffInfo.value: A firegeist can shine brightly or be primarily smoky and dark, as it wishes. It always sheds a little light.

traits.name: Elemental Nature

traits.name: Variable Illumination

traits.name: Water Susceptibility

If the target is a creature, the target must succeed on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw or ignite. Until a creature takes an action to douse the fire, the target takes 3 (**1d6**) fire damage at the start of each of its turns.

The target must make a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, the target takes 14 (**4d6**) fire damage and is frightened for 1 minute. On a success, the target takes half the damage and isn't frightened. While frightened, the creature takes 3 (**1d6**) fire damage at the start of each of its turns. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

fluffInfo.value: These foot-and-a-half-long wasps are a seasonal pest around Alderheart, drawn to the tree in the summer months by the blooming of giant orchids known as witherhearts. They are named for their red-orange coloration, as well as for the burning pain caused by their venom. Firelances are easily provoked and quick to sting. Firelances possess a potent venom that is coveted by assassins for both its availability and its lethality.

fluffInfo.value: *This obese, bell-shaped giant is blemished by ulcers, enlarged veins, and fungal rashes. Though it stumbles about on a pair of short, calloused legs, it moves its weight with dangerous potential.*

fluffInfo.name: Great Girth
fluffInfo.value: Whether as a result of a centuries-past curse or a gradual adaptation to an easygoing existence, the flab giant is gigantic in width rather than height and almost comical in its simple life. Too obese to effectively grasp weapons in its chubby fingers, a flab giant uses its great mass to deadly effect, overrunning or grabbing opponents and then sitting on them to crush them to death. Its bulk and hardiness allow it to tolerate the blows of struggling victims until they are fully crushed.

fluffInfo.name: Efficient Foragers
fluffInfo.value: Flab giants are the least active of giant types, spending most of their waking hours resting, napping, and sleeping, and only devote a short period each day to listlessly shuffling about, scrounging for food. Because a flab giant can eat practically anything, it doesn't have to roam far to find enough food to sustain its bulk, and only devote a short period each day to listlessly shuffling about, scrounging for food. Because a flab giant can eat practically anything, it doesn't have to roam far to find enough food to sustain its bulk, and it is rarely found far from its crude lair

fluffInfo.name: Knotted Skins
fluffInfo.value: Flab giants wear only scraps of clothing made of loosely knotted skins, leaving most of their stretch-marked and discolored skin exposed. Favored pelts include bear and human. A flab giant stands eight to ten feet tall and weighs 2,000 to 2,500 pounds.

traits.name: Massive Bulk
traits.value: A flab giant can't take the Dash action. In addition, a creature attempting to grapple, push, or knock the giant prone has disadvantage on attack rolls and ability checks to do so.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The giant makes two Slam attacks. If both attacks hit a Medium or smaller creature, the target is grappled (escape DC 15).

actions.name: Slam
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 12 (**2d6 + 5**) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Squatting Pin

On a failure, a creature takes 22 (**5d6 + 5**) bludgeoning damage and is restrained until the grapple ends. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn't restrained, but it remains grappled until it escapes. While restrained, a creature takes 8 (**1d6 + 5**) bludgeoning damage at the start of each of the giant's turns. If the flab giant moves, the target is no longer restrained or grappled.

fluffInfo.value: *The dragon bears black scales, more charred than naturally colored. Cracks between the scales glow a dull red, until the dragon rears its head and roars. Red embers become bright orange flames as the creature lights up from tail to maw*.Flame dragons are capricious creatures, fascinated by dark emotions and destructive passions. The dragons of eternal fire are proud and jealous, quick to anger, and utterly unforgiving. They bring total ruin to entire civilizations for trivial reasons, but their true motivation is the fun to be had. These burning serpents treat rage, deceit, and despair as toys for their amusement. "May you be the fire's plaything" is a curse often used by the foolish.

fluffInfo.name: Taunting Others
fluffInfo.value: The hot-blooded creatures tease their victims like cats, seeing the world and all within it as their rightful prey. Young flame dragons are less subtle than their elders. Wyrmlings may force a woman to watch her family die or ruin a beautiful face for pleasure—direct and evil. As the dragon matures, this natural sadism develops into a desire for more complicated sport. Aging dragons of fire use politics, murder, and magic in elaborate schemes only their ilk can appreciate. Many create plots so intricate and layered that they lack a true resolution, creating only endless manipulation. A hero might foil an assassination only to see the king thus saved become a despot. She might defeat the vizier whispering lies in the ruler's ear only to discover he was a pawn in a vast conspiracy. Dark ambitions, poisoned daggers, and old vendettas build such momentum that one scheme begins each time another ends. Often, even killing the draconic mastermind cannot extinguish the fires it started.

fluffInfo.name: Malevolent Purpose
fluffInfo.value: The results of a flame dragon's schemes are secondary to the enjoyment it derives from pursuing a nebulous and ever-changing goal. Some flame dragons spend centuries torturing a family line for nothing more than trespassing on the dragon's land. Others plot eternal curses after twisting poorly chosen words into dire insults. The vengeance itself is secondary to an excuse for hate, plot, and ruin. Flame dragons relish such opportunities for revenge. Each is a delightful hobby. Any disruption in their game kindles a terrible rage, and in these rare moments of defeat, their anger can be catastrophic. Entire cities burn.

fluffInfo.name: Fond of Souvenirs
fluffInfo.value: Flame dragons are as materialistic and territorial as other true dragons. Each pursues an individual obsession it fixates upon with mad devotion to fill its hoard. Some corrupt innocence, others push nations to war, but they always collect a memento for each victory, petty or grand. One might collect scorched skulls, while another saves the melted treasures of toppled empires. When not out sowing discord, the ancient flame dragons enjoy contemplating their hoards. Every piece reminds them of their own majesty and genius.

fluffInfo.name: Vengeful Brethren
fluffInfo.value: Nothing is safe from a flame dragon's scheming and narcissism. They crave absolute attention and constant reassurance. Anyone who humiliates a flame dragon would be wiser to kill it. Its survival ensures the dragon's undivided attention for generations. Wiser still, is to remove all trace of involvement in a flame dragon's death. All burning serpents see the murder of one of their kin as the gravest insult.

actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +3 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 6 (**1d10 + 1**) piercing damage plus 3 (**1d6**) fire damage.

actions.name: Fire Breath (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: The dragon exhales fire in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw, taking 17 (**5d6**) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

actions.name: Radiant Flames

fluffInfo.name: Flaming Skeleton
fluffInfo.value: The skeletal remains of many of those who opposed Thordak the Cinder King are said to be forever imbued with the primordial power of his fire breath. Areas scarred by the red dragon's power, including Thordak's Crater in Emon's Cloudtop District, the Ashen Gorge in the Stormcrest Mountains, and Serpent's Head in the Cliffkeep Mountains, are rife with flaming skeletons. These undead react to the raw power of the Elemental Planes, and are filled with an unquenchable desire to spread flames far and wide until nothing is left untouched by fire.
