If she does so, the creature has disadvantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects for 24 hours.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The Queen of Witches makes three Moonsilver Ring attacks or four Mystical Blast attacks. She can replace one attack with a use of spellcasting. If she hits one creature with two Mystical Blast attacks, the target must succeed on a DC 20 Strength saving throw or be pushed up to 10 feet away from her.

actions.name: Moonsilver Ring
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +12 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. *Hit:* 15 (**2d8 + 6**) slashing damage plus 7 (**2d6**) radiant damage.

actions.name: Mystical Blast
actions.value: *Melee or Ranged Spell Attack:* +12 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft., one target. *Hit:* 16 (**3d6 + 6**) force damage.

actions.name: Spray of Moonlight (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: The Queen of Witches sends moonlight flooding out from her. Each creature within 15 feet of her must make a DC 20 Dexterity saving throw, taking 42 (**12d6**) radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. If the Queen is standing in an area of moonlight when she uses this action, each creature in the area has disadvantage on the saving throw. A creature that fails the saving throw by 5 or more is blinded until the end of its next turn.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (4/Day)
traits.value: If the jotun fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.value: The jotun has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Material Bound
traits.value: The jotun has Immunity to any spell or effect that would force it to leave the Material Plane, unless the jotun wants to leave. It has Disadvantage on saving throws against effects that would return it to the Material Plane from another plane of existence.

traits.name: Too Big to Notice
traits.value: While the jotun remains motionless in nonmagical, natural terrain, it has Advantage on Dexterity (*Stealth*) checks.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The jotun makes three Greatclub or Rock attacks in any combination. Instead of one of those attacks, it can use Icy Sweep or cast Fear.

actions.name: Greatclub
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +17 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. *Hit:* 28 (**4d8 + 10**) Bludgeoning damage plus 27 (**6d8**) Cold damage.

actions.name: Rock
actions.value: *Ranged Attack Roll:* +17 to hit, range 60/240 ft., one target. *Hit:* 32 (**4d10 + 10**) Bludgeoning damage plus 27 (**6d8**) Cold damage.

actions.name: Icy Sweep (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: *Dexterity Saving Throw:* DC 23 Each creature within 20 feet of the jotun. *Failure:* 36 (**8d8**) Bludgeoning damage and 54 (**12d8**) Cold damage, and the target is pushed up to 15 feet away from the jotun and has the Prone condition. *Success* Half damage only.

fluffInfo.value: *This silver sphere, polished to a mirror-like sheen bobs gently in the air for a moment before suddenly flattening out into a round, serrated blade.*

The quicksilver siege orb is an alchemical construct designed for use as a siege weapon. The orb measures 3 feet in diameter and weighs 30 pounds. When it changes to disk form, its diameter increases to 6 feet, but it is only an inch thin.

fluffInfo.name: Smart Silver
fluffInfo.value: Arcanists replicated a semi-sentient quicksilver they found in the underworld and provided it to warring factions. The metal changes its disposition to match its form. As an orb, it is contemplative and observant. As a blade, it is aggressive, seeking to kill enemy combatants. Fortunately, it takes commands well and avoids inflicting collateral damage.

fluffInfo.name: Autonomous Siege Weapon
fluffInfo.value: A quicksilver siege orb can fit into a catapult or other throwing siege weapon while in spherical form. When it reaches its destination, it hovers in place to assess soft targets before changing into its disk form and injuring or killing those targets.

fluffInfo.name: Customizable Alternate Form
fluffInfo.value: Though the siege orb can have only one alternate form, the orb accepts instructions for several shapes beyond the standard whirling disk, such as spiked balls, borers, and other devices useful in battle.

entries: **Resistances**: fire, lightning; piercing, slashing from nonmagical attacks
**Immunities**: bludgeoning, poison, psychic; charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, unconscious
**Languages**: understands one language of its creator but can't speak

traits.name: Bludgeoning Bounce (Orb Form Only)
traits.value: Whenever the quicksilver siege orb is subjected to bludgeoning damage, it takes no damage and instead is pushed up to 15 feet away from the source of the bludgeoning damage. If the damage is from a critical hit, the orb is pushed up to 30 feet.

traits.name: Construct Nature
traits.value: The quicksilver siege orb doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

traits.name: Flyby
traits.value: The quicksilver siege orb doesn't provoke opportunity attacks when it flies out of an enemy's reach.

traits.name: Immutable Form
traits.value: The quicksilver siege orb is immune to any spell or effect that would alter its form.

traits.name: Observant (Orb Form Only)
traits.value: The quicksilver siege orb has advantage on Wisdom (*Perception*) and Wisdom (*Insight*) checks. In addition, if the orb observes a creature for at least 1 minute, it has advantage on the first three attack rolls it makes against the creature.

traits.name: Slippery
traits.value: The quicksilver siege orb has advantage on saving throws and ability checks made to escape a grapple.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The quicksilver siege orb makes three Disk Blade or Slam attacks.

actions.name: Disk Blade (Disk Form Only)
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 12 (**2d6 + 5**) slashing damage.

actions.name: Slam (Orb Form Only)
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 10 (**2d4 + 5**) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Slashing Run (Recharge 4-6)
actions.value: The quicksilver siege orb flies up to 20 feet in a straight line, then it flies up to 20 feet in a straight line in a different direction. During this move, it can move through the space of any Large or smaller creature. The first time it enters a creature's space during this move, that creature must make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw, taking 35 (**10d6**) slashing damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

bonusActions.name: Shape Quicksilver
bonusActions.value: The quicksilver siege orb flattens itself into a razor-sharp, whirling disk or back into its orb form. Its statistics are the same in each form. It becomes a puddle of quicksilver if it dies.

entries: **Resistances**: bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from nonmagical attacks that aren't adamantine (Hardened Form only)
**Languages**: Deep Speech, Terran; may know either Common or Goblin

traits.name: False Appearance
traits.value: While the gargoyle remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from an inanimate statue.

traits.name: Quickstone Body
traits.value: At the start of its turn, if it does not have the Incapacitated condition, the gargoyle can choose whether it adopts a Hardened or Softened Form, each of which grants bonuses.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The gargoyle makes one Bite attack and one Claw attack.

actions.name: Bite
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +5, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 6 (**1d6 + 3**) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Claw
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +5, reach 5 ft. (15 ft. in Softened Form) *Hit:* 7 (**1d8 + 3**) Slashing damage (12 (**2d8 + 3**) Slashing damage in Hardened Form).

bonusActions.name: Fluid Form (Softened Form Only)
bonusActions.value: The gargoyle takes the Dodge action.

bonusActions.name: Remold
bonusActions.value: The gargoyle transforms into a Medium Humanoid, Humanoid statue it has seen, or back into its true form. Its statistics are the same in each form, though it still appears to be made of stone, except that it loses its Fly Speed if it takes the shape of a Humanoid without wings. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed. The gargoyle can choose to reshape its claws to resemble melee weapons of its choice. The damage dice remain the same, but when it takes a new form it can choose to deal Piercing or Bludgeoning damage instead of Slashing damage. It reverts to its true form if it dies.

fluffInfo.value: *The reeking creature resembles a toothless, cadaverous hag. Its large eyes glow with unearthly green light, and ragged claws extend from its fingers.*

fluffInfo.name: Twisted Nymphs
fluffInfo.value: Qwyllion (the name means "polluter" in Old Elvish) are fey who have been twisted by the corrupted magic of magical wastelands or warped by alchemical experiments into baleful versions of their former selves.

fluffInfo.name: Frighten Animals
fluffInfo.value: Besides making them hideously ugly, the transformation leaves them with a deadly gaze and the ability to control a living creature with a mere glance. Most animals can sense the corruption within the fey and refuse to approach it.

fluffInfo.name: Goblin Mercenaries
fluffInfo.value: Qwyllion are sometimes engaged by goblin sorcerers and evil mages to guard desecrated temples and despoiled gardens. The terms and payments for these arrangements vary wildly from one qwyllion to the next. Anyone who dares to employ a qwyllion must be constantly vigilant, because these creatures are prone to renege on any agreement eventually.

entries: **Resistances**: acid, fire; bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from nonmagical attacks
**Languages**: Common, Goblin, Infernal, Sylvan, Void Speech

traits.name: Nauseating Stench
traits.value: A creature that starts its turn within 20 feet of the qwyllion must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 1 minute. A poisoned creature that fails this saving throw is also incapacitated while poisoned in this way. A poisoned creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If a creature's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is immune to the qwyllion's Nauseating Stench for the next 24 hours.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The qwyllion makes three Claw or Deadly Gaze attacks. If two Deadly Gaze attacks hit one creature, the target must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or be incapacitated until the end of its next turn.

actions.name: Claw
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 18 (**3d8 + 5**) slashing damage.

actions.name: Deadly Gaze
actions.value: *Ranged Spell Attack:* +6 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. *Hit:* 17 (**4d6 + 3**) psychic damage. A Humanoid slain by this attack rises 8 hours later as a specter under the qwyllion's control, unless the Humanoid is restored to life. The qwyllion can have no more than ten specters under its control at one time.

actions.name: Charm
actions.value: One Humanoid or Beast the qwyllion can see within 30 feet of it must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw or be magically charmed for 1 day. The charmed target obeys the qwyllion's verbal commands. If the target suffers any harm or receives a suicidal command, it can repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on a success. If the target successfully saves against the effect, or if the effect on it ends, the target is immune to the qwyllion's Charm for the next 24 hours.
The qwyllion can have no more than one Humanoid and up to three Beasts charmed at a time. If it charms another Humanoid or a fourth Beast, the oldest effect on a previous target ends.

fluffInfo.value: *Poised in thoughtful contemplation is an androgenous, elfin figure holding an intricately wrought spyglass. White-gold curls fall to their shoulders, and their brow is encircled by motes of light that glow like stars. Their outfit is a crisp white suit but overlayed with a sash colored with the pink and orange ombré of a painted sky ready to greet the rising sun*.

The honorably appointed Radiant Chancellor Ectius, ambassador to the stars, is a steadfast advisor to the Court of One Million Stars. The Radiant Chancellor has served the court since its inception, long before the ruling Prince Valendan ascended to rulership. While it is strange that such an ancient and capable fey would acquiesce to the dominion of another, anyone who meets Ectius immediately understands where their true ambition lies.

fluffInfo.name: Pursuit of Knowledge
fluffInfo.value: Ectius is obsessed with the beauty and radiant power given to stars. Over the thousands of years they have existed, Ectius has sacrificed material pleasures, social status, and personal identity to pursue ultimate cosmic knowledge. The chancellor's efforts have been rewarded, for they have learned hundreds of true names for the stars that hang in the heavens. With the acquisition of each name, Ectius grows in power, for to know a star's true name is to have dominion over them. For now, the Radiant Chancellor is content to serve and advise the members of the royal court.

entries: **Resistances**: cold; bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from attacks not made with cold iron weapons
**Languages**: Celestial, Common, Elvish, Sylvan, telepathy 100 ft., Umbral

traits.name: Cloak of Dawn
traits.value: When a creature that can see the radiant lord starts its turn within 60 feet of them, the radiant lord can force it to make a DC 19 Constitution saving throw if the radiant lord isn't incapacitated and can see the creature. If the saving throw fails, the creature is stunned until the beginning of its next turn.

Unless *surprised*, a creature can avert its eyes to avoid the saving throw at the start of its turn. If the creature does so, it can't see the radiant lord until the start of its next turn, when it can avert its eyes again. If the creature looks at the radiant lord in the meantime, it must immediately make the save.

traits.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
traits.value: If the radiant lord fails a saving throw, they can choose to succeed instead.

traits.name: Lord of Light
traits.value: Whenever the radiant lord deals damage, they can choose to change the damage type to radiant. Additionally, creatures that would normally be immune to radiant damage are only resistant to radiant damage dealt by the radiant lord.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.value: The radiant lord has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The radiant lord makes two Starmetal Saber attacks or one Starmetal Saber attack and one Spellcasting attack.

actions.name: Starmetal Saber
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +11 to hit, range 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 11 (**2d8 + 2**) slashing damage plus 10 (**3d6**) radiant damage. This is a magical weapon that counts as cold iron for the purpose of overcoming damage resistance.

actions.name: Comet Shot
actions.value: *Ranged Spell Attack:* +11 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. *Hit:* 27 (**5d10**) radiant damage, and the target begins to glow with starlight. The radiant lord has advantage on the next attack roll made against a glowing target.

actions.name: Dazzling Presence
actions.value: Each creature of the radiant lord's choice that is within 120 feet of the radiant lord and aware of them must succeed on a DC 19 Constitution saving throw or become blinded for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If a creature's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is immune to the radiant lord's Dazzling Presence for the next 24 hours.

actions.name: Meteor Shower (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: Falling stars hit the ground in a 20-foot-radius, 40-foot-high cylinder centered on a point the radiant lord can see within 300 feet. Each creature in the cylinder must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 28 (**8d6**) bludgeoning damage and 35 (**10d6**) radiant damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

traits.name: Exploit Opening (3/Day)
traits.value: When Radlee makes an attack, she has advantage on the attack roll.

traits.name: Sure-Footed
traits.value: Radlee has advantage on saving throws against being moved against her will or knocked prone.

traits.name: Tactical Vigilance
traits.value: Radlee has advantage on initiative checks.
While she isn't incapacitated, Radlee and each ally within 30 feet of her who can see or hear her can't be surprised.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: Radlee makes three Halberd or three Longbow attacks. Alternatively, she makes one Halberd attack and uses Backswipe.

actions.name: Halberd
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +10 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. *Hit:* 12 (**1d10 + 7**) slashing damage.

actions.name: Longbow
actions.value: *Ranged Weapon Attack:* +6 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one target. *Hit:* 7 (**1d8 + 3**) piercing damage.

actions.name: Backswipe
actions.value: Radlee swings her halberd's shaft at a creature within 5 feet of her. The target must succeed on a DC 18 Strength saving throw or take 16 (**3d10**) bludgeoning damage and be knocked prone.

traits.name: Cat's Grace
traits.value: When the rakitten falls and isn't incapacitated, it can subtract up to 30 feet from the fall when calculating falling damage. In addition, it has advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to avoid the prone condition.

traits.name: Swipey
traits.value: While not in combat, the rakitten takes any opportunity it can to knock things off shelves and ledges.

actions.name: Claw
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 4 (**1d4 + 2**) slashing damage.

actions.name: Ethereal Paw
actions.value: A spectral, magical, floating paw appears at a point the rakitten chooses within 30 feet of it. The paw lasts for 1 minute or until the rakitten dismisses it as a bonus action. The paw vanishes if it is ever more than 30 feet away from the rakitten or if the rakitten uses this action again.

The rakitten can use its action to control the paw. It can use the paw to manipulate an object, open an unlocked door or container, stow or retrieve an item from an open container, or pour the contents out of a vial. It can move the paw up to 30 feet each time it uses it. The paw can't attack, activate magic items, or carry more than 10 pounds.

fluffInfo.value: [she/her]

Raleigh Burrowbright (__jerbeen swashbuckler__) is Skopps' first mate. She is a bold jerbeen who has proven herself loyal to __Skopps__ through many daring deeds. She had seen Skopps' power over animals and trusts him completely. Her loyalty to her leader is absolute if perhaps misplaced.

traits.name: Standing Leap
traits.value: The swashbuckler's base long jump is 30 feet, and their base high jump is 15 feet, with or without a running start.

traits.name: Team Tactics
traits.value: The swashbuckler can take the Help action as a bonus action.

traits.name: Sharp Witted Defense
traits.value: While the swashbuckler is wearing light or no armor and wielding no shield, their AC includes their Charisma modifier.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The swashbuckler makes three attacks, one with a dagger and two with their rapier.

actions.name: Dagger
actions.value: *Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack:* +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. *Hit:* 6 (**1d4 + 4**) piercing damage.

actions.name: Rapier
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 8 (**1d8 + 4**) piercing damage.

fluffInfo.value: *The especially lanky man with long limbs and thick locks of hair traced magical symbols with delicate fingers, opening a small portal.*

The ramag were a powerful tribe of dimensional sorcerers allied with a great society of titans, and they were indeed human in ages past. Over time, strange practices warped them into their current state, and they are clearly no longer purely human. They have angular features, and their limbs grow long in proportion to their bodies, giving them a stooped posture. A ramag's hair is impossibly thick, each strand being the width of a human finger, which they wear tied back with decorative clasps.

*The ramag all live within the twelve scattered districts of their home city, Ramagani (home, in their dialect), with eleven districts in the Abandoned Lands of the Southlands and one on an island off the coast. Though the districts are far apart, the ramag consider them all part of one great metropolis. The inhabited districts are guarded by powerful ramag spellcasters and by the Stormwatch—a garrison of arcane warriors who operate enchanted lightning ballistae in defense of the city. A lightning ballista functions identically to a standard ballista but does an additional 1d10 lightning damage with each hit.*

fluffInfo.name: Portal Network
fluffInfo.value: The ramag used their innate magical gifts and affinity for portals to maintain powerful magical conduits. This mastery of the arcane allowed instantaneous travel to the farthest-flung outpost. The ramag still maintain a network of magical monoliths that connect the scattered districts of their home, but this network is frayed and fading.

fluffInfo.name: Studious and Powerful
fluffInfo.value: Although physically weak, the ramag are sharp-witted, studious, and naturally infused with magic. Lifetimes of exposure to the warping effect of their runaway magical energy have given them innate control over magic as well as sharp resistance to it. They are acutely aware of their responsibility for keeping magic in check and fully know the danger of uncontrolled magical energies. Even the lowliest ramag has a keen intellect and a natural understanding of magic. Many ramag take up the study of wizardry. Few become wandering adventurers, but well-equipped expeditions sometimes leave their homeland to inspect the surrounding countryside.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.value: The ramag has advantage on saving throws against spells or other magical effects.

traits.name: Portal Sense
traits.value: The ramag can pinpoint the location of planar portals within 100 feet of it and can sense the general direction of planar portals within 1 mile of it. In addition, if the ramag spends 10 minutes studying a portal, it can determine the portal's destination and any requirements to use or activate it.

actions.name: Scimitar
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 5 (**1d6 + 2**) slashing damage.

actions.name: Shortbow
actions.value: *Ranged Weapon Attack:* +4 to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. *Hit:* 5 (**1d6 + 2**) piercing damage.

bonusActions.name: Portal Traveler (Recharge 5-6)
bonusActions.value: The ramag creates and steps into a small portal and out of an identical portal in a space it can see within 60 feet of it. If a creature is in the destination space, the creature must make a DC 13 Intelligence saving throw. On a failure, the ramag trades spaces with the creature. On a success, the ramag fails to teleport. Whatever the result, the portal disappears.

actions.name: Pact Blade
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +4, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 6 (**1d8 + 2**) Slashing damage plus 7 (**2d6**) Necrotic damage.

traits.name: Land's Stride
traits.value: Moving through nonmagical difficult terrain costs the ranger no extra movement. It can also pass through nonmagical plants without being slowed by them and without taking damage from them if they have thorns, spines, or a similar hazard.

actions.name: Multiattack

actions.name: Longbow

actions.name: Volley
actions.value: The ranger makes a separate Longbow attack against each creature of its choice within 10 feet of a point it can see within the weapon's range.

actions.name: Whirlwind
actions.value: The ranger makes a separate Shortsword attack against each creature of its choice within its reach.

bonusActions.name: Hunter's Mark (1/Short or Long Rest)
bonusActions.value: The ranger chooses one creature it can see within 90 feet and mystically marks it as its quarry for 1 hour. For the duration, the ranger deals an extra 3 (**1d6**) damage to the target whenever it hits it with a weapon attack, and the ranger has advantage on any Wisdom (*Perception*) or Wisdom (*Survival*) check it makes to find the creature. If the target drops to 0 hit points before this effect ends, the ranger can use a bonus action on a subsequent turn to mark a new creature.

fluffInfo.value: The crew of the pirate poacher Skopps the Beast-Breaker is made up of maran raptors who are as skilled in nautical exploration as they are in combat.

It lands in an unoccupied space at the end of its movement, and takes no falling damage. The deckhand can't glide while carrying heavy objects, heavy weapons, or shields (though it can drop any held items as part of its reaction).

fluffInfo.value: Freebooters are skilled smugglers and skirmishers who can be found in the employ of only the most successful pirate crews. While their loyalty is easily secured with coin, most will abandon their captain or seek to mutiny if they lose faith in their captain's ability to keep their pockets filled.

It lands in an unoccupied space at the end of its movement, and takes no falling damage. The mercenary can't glide while carrying heavy objects, heavy weapons, or shields (though it can drop any held items as part of its reaction).

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: Leading other ratlings into battle, the Rat Prince is a ferocious combatant. He uses his Sacrificial Pawn Reaction to avoid attacks while firing his crossbow or attacking ferociously with his Contaminated Bite. He uses Ratling Cunning to ensure that he remains adjacent to another ratling he can use as a body shield.

Caught alone, the Rat Prince doesn't fight: he flees. If he can't, he cries and begs for his life. He will sell out other ratlings if it means his own survival. When this rat is cornered, he offers anything he can think of to convince characters to let him go free, and will claim he can lead characters to fantastic treasures, secret passages through the city, vast amounts of "the shiny," and boasts that his favorable reputation amongst the ratlings can guarantee safety. Whether or not these are true is up to you. Unless the characters can make the Rat Prince loyal in some other way (through food, fear, or magic), he tries to escape at the earliest opportunity.

actions.name: The Rat Crown-Prince always takes his turn on Initiative count 20
actions.value: On his turn, The Rat Crown Prince can use his movement and interaction as normal. However, he does not take an action or Bonus Action on his turn unless forced to do so by a spell or other effect. Instead, the Rat Crown-Prince takes one of the following Epic Actions at the end of each player character's turn:

actions.name: Contaminated Bite (1/Round)
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +10, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 8 (**1d4 + 6**) Piercing damage plus 10 (**3d6**) Necrotic damage. *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 15. *Failure:* The target gains one Contamination level.

actions.name: Delerium-Infused Blades
actions.value: *Melee or Ranged Attack Roll:* +10, reach 5 ft. or range 30/60 ft. *Hit:* 13 (**2d6 + 6**) Necrotic damage, and the target suffers one of the following effects of the Rat Crown-Prince's choice (he can't select the same option more than once per round):

entries: **Poison**: *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 16. *Failure:* 18 (**4d8**) Poison damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition for 1 minute (save ends). *Success* Half damage only.
**Acid Burn**: *Dexterity Saving Throw:* DC 16. *Failure:* 10 (**3d6**) Acid damage, and the target has the Burning condition (3d6 Acid). *Success* Half damage only.
**Mindkiller**: If the target is maintaining *Concentration* on a spell, it takes an extra 25 (**5d10**) Psychic damage unless it chooses to end its *Concentration*.

actions.name: Call Ratlings (1/Round)
actions.value: 2d4 __Ratling Warriors__ appear, burrowing up from below unoccupied spaces within 60 feet of the Rat Crown-Prince. The warriors have 1 Hit Point each and remain until killed.

actions.name: Meld into Shadow (1/Round)
actions.value: The Rat Crown-Prince has the Invisible condition until he makes an attack.

actions.name: Swift Stride
actions.value: The Rat Crown-Prince moves up to his Speed.

actions.name: Epic Resistance
actions.value: The Rat Crown-Prince chooses one condition, spell, or other effect currently affecting him and rolls 1d20. On an 11+, the effect ends on him. The Rat Crown-Prince can use this action even if he would otherwise be unable to take actions, his actions are being controlled by another creature, or if a spell or effect alters his game statistics.

fluffInfo.name: Roleplaying Traits
fluffInfo.value: The Rat God has destructive and apocalyptic motivations.

entries: **Personality Trait:** You seem hungry. Are you hungry?
**Ideal:** Eat or be eaten. That is the way of things. Eat! Eat! Eat! It is all food when you need to survive!
**Bond:** What you have is not enough. If you kill and eat them all. What was theirs is now yours!
**Flaw:** Why does your friend get to have nicer things than you? Don't you deserve them instead? Betray them! Eat them! Make it yours!

fluffInfo.name: (20+) Fiendish Power
fluffInfo.value: You are aware of its Truesight and telepathy, its Resistances and Immunities, and its Epic Resistance. You also know this Rat God is beyond life and death and can reform years later if killed

fluffInfo.name: (25+) Cloud of Rats
fluffInfo.value: You are aware of the creature's Verminous Aura trait.

fluffInfo.name: (30+) Powerful Presence
fluffInfo.value: You know Rat God's highest and lowest ability scores and saving throws.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: The Rat God is a being of pure malice and appetite. It cares not for the whims of mortals, only for pure destruction and the chattering and gnawing of infinite rats as they devour the cosmos. It finds joy only in annihilation, and the screams of mortals as they are reduced to bone by the Rat God's writhing swarm.

The Rat God can use its Rodent Rift to move to where it can catch as many targets as possible in its Verminous Aura, then set them ablaze with its Flail of Skulls. It will target the weakest characters with its Warp Bolt, and the least intelligent with its Infernal Chittering. It performs a Great Feeding to replenish itself and uses Rodent Rifts to escape a dangerous situation.

entries: **Flail of Skulls**: *Melee Attack Roll:* +16, reach 15 ft. *Hit:* 28 (**3d12 + 9**) Bludgeoning damage, and the target has the Burning condition (3d6 Acid).

fluffInfo.name: Plague and Dark Magic

Rats afflicted with virulent leavings of dark magic rites or twisted experiments become bound to one another. As more rats add to the mass, the creature's intelligence and force of will grow.

fluffInfo.name: Sleek-Furred Celestials
fluffInfo.value: The ratatosk is a celestial being that is very much convinced of its own indispensable place in the multiverse. Its fur is sleek, and it takes great pride in the cleaning and maintenance of its tusks.

fluffInfo.name: Planar Messengers
fluffInfo.value: Ratatosks were created to carry messages across the planes, bearing word between gods and their servants. Somewhere across the vast march of ages, their nature twisted away from that purpose. Much speculation as to the exact cause of this change continues to occupy sages.

fluffInfo.name: Maddening Gossips
fluffInfo.value: Ratatosks are insatiable tricksters. Their constant chatter is not the mere nattering of their animal counterparts; it is a never-ending celestial gossip network. Ratatosks delight in learning secrets and spreading those secrets in mischievous ways. It's common for two listeners to hear vastly different words when a ratatosk speaks—and for that misunderstanding to lead to blows.

actions.name: Divisive Chatter (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: The ratatosk causes division and strife in up to four creatures it can see within 30 feet of it. Each target must succeed on a DC 14 Charisma saving throw or be irritated for 1 minute. While irritated, a creature must spend its action on each of its turns arguing with, complaining about, or otherwise expressing unhappiness toward one of its allies over a trivial matter. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

fluffInfo.value: *The halfling-sized, furred creature has a twitching snout, bony feet, and a long, pink tail.*

The ratfolk are canny survivors, rogues, and tricksters. Their strong family ties make it easy for them to found or join criminal societies—though others serve as expert scouts and saboteurs, able to infiltrate army camps, city sewers, and even castle dungeons with equal ease. Ratfolk leaders are often spellcasters and rogues.

fluffInfo.name: Adaptable
fluffInfo.value: Ratfolk swim well and can survive on little. Some groups are endemic to tropical and subtropical islands. Others inhabit forests, sewers, labyrinths, and ancient, ruined cities.

fluffInfo.name: Fast Fighters
fluffInfo.value: Ratfolk prefer light weapons and armor, fighting with speed and using numbers to bring down a foe. They have been known to ally themselves with goblins, darakhul, and kobolds on occasion, but more often prefer to serve a "Rat King" who may or may not be a rat of any kind. Such rat rulers might include a wererat, a rat king, an ogre, a minor demon, or an intelligent undead.

traits.value: The ratfolk can move through the space of any Medium or larger hostile creature, and such a space isn't difficult terrain for the ratfolk.

fluffInfo.value: *A pair of glinting yellow-purple eyes appear down the dark tunnel ahead, then another, then more. A scurrying mass of furry bodies bound up in mud-spattered cloth and greasy leather surge forward. Their rodent-like claws brandish rust-caked blades as many squeaking voices erupt into a cacophony of chittering, chirping, screeching, and finally a howl of "Kill! Kill! Kill!"*

Ratlings are oversized mutated rats imbued with malevolent cunning and driven by a mad compulsion to consume and multiply. These wretched monsters suffer from a constant internal struggle between cowardly survival instincts and violent impulsive urges. Ratlings dream of eating everything, and will eat anything, but love eating people. They especially love eating babies. While they will subsist on carrion, ratlings take captives back to their lairs so they can have fresh food later. Thousands of ratlings dwell in the city. They form warring colonies that dig maze-like burrows featuring multiple entrances and tight looping passages. Successful colonies grow in number quickly, as ratlings mature in a matter of weeks when ample food and delerium are available.

They are likely to position themselves on rooftops or behind rubble, and often secure their locations with pit traps, flasks of oil, torches, or other devious traps when they are able. Once they notice their target is in position, Ratling Guttersnipes unload a volley of poison-tipped bolts, or unleash deadly traps. After their targets are weakened, the ratlings rushes in to surprise and stab creatures with their delerium blades, and then quickly dart back out.
As with all ratlings, if the fight turns against them, they will flee or beg for their lives.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: Ratlings fight together in large groups to surround and overwhelm their foes with Pack Tactics. They use whatever rusty weapons they can find, or use their teeth and claws when nothing else is available. Occasionally, ratlings carry makeshift slings and hurl anything they pick up off the ground at their enemies: rocks, bones, or even chips of delerium.

However, ratlings flee and hide using Ratling Cunning when they don't have a numerical advantage over their foes. Indeed, they won't start fights if they don't outnumber their foes at least two to one, but while they outnumber their foes three to one or more, the typical ratling warrior can become insanely brave. When ratlings overpower their foes, they may even grapple them down and take them as prisoners to eat later.

fluffInfo.name: Ravager Slaughter Lord
fluffInfo.value: Some warlords of the Dividing Plains, hungry for recognition in the single burning eye of their god, turn to the Ravagers in the name of blood and glory. Those few whose deeds live up to their ambitions soon find themselves leading factions of the cult—and honored by the title of Slaughter Lord. A Slaughter Lord craves combat and leads Ravager raids as often as possible. However, they are frequently forced to remain at their strongholds because of the strict regimen of alchemical treatments that grant them increased power.

A small army of shamans and alchemists attend to the Slaughter Lords to artificially enhance their strength and fury, creating concoctions to grow their muscular forms to massive size, sharpen their tactical reasoning, and bestow upon them the divine protection of the __The Ruiner__. A Slaughter Lord's unnatural size is their most obvious martial advantage, enabling them to dual-wield even the largest weapons. But the __The Ruiner__ blessings also grant them access to divine magic that can blind or slay enemies with a word.
It is speculated that four major arms of the Ravagers are each commanded by one of these terrors, but the exact number of Slaughter Lords remains unknown.

fluffInfo.name: Ravager Stabby-Stabber
fluffInfo.value: Adventurers and mercenaries most often take up arms against the Ravagers after hearing stories of the hordes terrorizing the free peoples of the Dividing Plains. They prepare themselves for brutal combat against even more brutal foes—and are thus unprepared for the Ravagers' most terrifying weapon, the stabby-stabbers. Fresh-faced warriors from Emon laugh at the name when they first hear it in Kymal's taverns, even as veteran mercenaries close their eyes and hastily bury their faces in their tankards.

Nimble Ravager warriors who show exceptional skill are brought before their Slaughter Lord and forced to drink a terrible brew the Ravagers call skullfire. This concoction burns away what little reasoning ability those warriors possessed, turning them into perfectly obedient, flesh-hungry monsters. In battle, stabby-stabbers swarm like rats, eviscerating enemies and bystanders alike.

fluffInfo.name: Leafy Advisors
fluffInfo.value: Wise and long-lived like treants, ravenalas tend their coastal forest homes far from most societies. Tribal humanoids respect and venerate ravenalas and sometimes seek their advice or aid in times of great need. Ravenalas seldom interact with others unless approached.

fluffInfo.name: Prisoner's Lamentation
fluffInfo.value: Unlike treants, ravenalas avoid physical conflict in favor of diplomacy and compromise. If annoyed, they imprison hostile creatures within their trunks rather than killing or eating the attackers. Trapped creatures must sing their own lament as they are carried off to a distant locale away from the ravenala's home.

traits.name: Magic Resistance

traits.name: Woodland Stride

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The ravenala makes two Bursting Pod or Slam attacks. If both Slam attacks hit a Medium or smaller creature, the target is grappled (escape DC 14), and the ravenala uses its Lamenting Engulfment on the target.

actions.name: Slam
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 18 (**3d8 + 5**) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Bursting Pod
actions.value: *Ranged Weapon Attack:* +8 to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. *Hit:* 12 (**2d6 + 5**) bludgeoning damage, and each creature within 5 feet of the target, including the target, must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw, taking 5 (**2d4**) piercing damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

actions.name: Lamenting Engulfment
actions.value: The ravenala engulfs a Medium or smaller creature grappled by it. The engulfed target is blinded and restrained, it has Cover against attacks and other effects outside the ravenala, and it must succeed on a DC 14 Charisma saving throw at the start of each of the ravenala's turns or sing a lament of the mistakes and misdeeds it has performed in its lifetime. While singing, the engulfed creature can still act, but it can't otherwise speak, including casting spells with verbal components. If the ravenala moves, the engulfed creature moves with it. The ravenala can have only one creature engulfed at a time.

actions.value: The ravenala removes a leaf from its head and wraps the leaf around the wounds of one creature it can see within 5 feet of it. The target magically regains 10 3d6 hp and is freed from any disease, poison, blindness, or deafness.

fluffInfo.value: *The creature's face resembles that of a great raven or crow, and it is covered in feathers from head to toe, though without wings.*

The ravenfolk are an avian race of scoundrels, schemers, and sneaks—but they are much more than that. Long ago when Odin brokered the truce that brought peace among the gods, the wily deity magically created the ravenfolk from feathers plucked from his ravens Huginn (Thought) and Muninn (Memory). He placed this new race into the world alongside elves, dwarves, humans, and others to be his eyes and ears.

*If the ravenfolk of Midgard have a homeland, it is Beldestan to the East, on a branch of Wotan's tree in the North, or a high cliff of Horus' hidden temple in the South. They have settlements in Trollheim, Vidim, Domovogrod, Zobeck, Nuria Natal, and the Dragon Empire, but none are large.*
*They avoid the West and the Seven Cities most of the time and are highly honored in Nuria Natal, where they serve the temples of Horus as sworn guardians, assassins, and seekers of forgotten arcana. Some are said to be members of the Emerald Order, a society devoted to arcane mysteries.*

fluffInfo.name: Odin's Children
fluffInfo.value: To this day, the ravenfolk are Odin's agents and embody his thought and memory. They are thieves of objects, yes, but primarily, they are thieves of secrets. Their black feathers and long beaks are spotted on the road from place to place, trading information or helping to hatch plots. They are widely viewed as spies, informers, thieves, and troublemakers, but when the ravenfolk swear an oath, they abide by it. Odin grants the best of his ravenfolk magical runespears and runestaves, weapons enchanted to serve his messengers. The ravenfolk consider them special tokens meant for their use, and no one else's.

fluffInfo.name: Flightless But Bold
fluffInfo.value: Though they have no wings and normally cannot fly, the physiology of ravenfolk is strikingly similar to that of true avians. They stand roughly 5 feet tall and, because of their hollow bones, weigh just 95–105 pounds. Albino ravenfolk are often found in southern climates. Ravenfolk eat almost anything, but they prefer raw meat and field grains, such as corn, soy, and alfalfa. They even scavenge days-old carrion, a practice that repulses most other humanoids.

fluffInfo.name: Feather Speech
fluffInfo.value: The ravenfolk have two languages: a verbal language full of croaks and whistles and a language of feathers. Ravenfolk can communicate volumes without speaking a word through the dyeing, arrangement, preening, and rustling of their plumage. This language is inherent to ravenfolk, and though others may use magic to understand it, it can't be used by creatures without feathers.

actions.value: The doom croaker furiously "beats" a set of phantasmal wings. Each creature within 5 feet of the ravenfolk must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or be blinded until the start of its next turn.

actions.name: Prophetic Magic
actions.value: The ravenfolk doom croaker can cast the __augury__ spell and __thaumaturgy__ cantrip at will, requiring no material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability.

actions.name: Prophetic Caw (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: The ravenfolk doom croaker caws a prophecy that sounds different to each listener. Each creature within 30 feet of the ravenfolk that can hear it must make a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw. Ravenfolk have advantage on the saving throw. On a failure, a creature hears a prophecy of its doom and is frightened for 1 minute. On a success, a creature hears a prophecy of its greatness and has advantage on the first attack roll it makes on each of its turns for 1 minute. A frightened creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

fluffInfo.value: *The creature's face resembles that of a great raven or crow, and it is covered in feathers from head to toe, though without wings.*

The ravenfolk are an avian race of scoundrels, schemers, and sneaks—but they are much more than that. Long ago when Odin brokered the truce that brought peace among the gods, the wily deity magically created the ravenfolk from feathers plucked from his ravens Huginn (Thought) and Muninn (Memory). He placed this new race into the world alongside elves, dwarves, humans, and others to be his eyes and ears.

*If the ravenfolk of Midgard have a homeland, it is Beldestan to the East, on a branch of Wotan's tree in the North, or a high cliff of Horus' hidden temple in the South. They have settlements in Trollheim, Vidim, Domovogrod, Zobeck, Nuria Natal, and the Dragon Empire, but none are large.*
*They avoid the West and the Seven Cities most of the time and are highly honored in Nuria Natal, where they serve the temples of Horus as sworn guardians, assassins, and seekers of forgotten arcana. Some are said to be members of the Emerald Order, a society devoted to arcane mysteries.*

fluffInfo.name: Odin's Children
fluffInfo.value: To this day, the ravenfolk are Odin's agents and embody his thought and memory. They are thieves of objects, yes, but primarily, they are thieves of secrets. Their black feathers and long beaks are spotted on the road from place to place, trading information or helping to hatch plots. They are widely viewed as spies, informers, thieves, and troublemakers, but when the ravenfolk swear an oath, they abide by it. Odin grants the best of his ravenfolk magical runespears and runestaves, weapons enchanted to serve his messengers. The ravenfolk consider them special tokens meant for their use, and no one else's.

fluffInfo.name: Flightless But Bold
fluffInfo.value: Though they have no wings and normally cannot fly, the physiology of ravenfolk is strikingly similar to that of true avians. They stand roughly 5 feet tall and, because of their hollow bones, weigh just 95–105 pounds. Albino ravenfolk are often found in southern climates. Ravenfolk eat almost anything, but they prefer raw meat and field grains, such as corn, soy, and alfalfa. They even scavenge days-old carrion, a practice that repulses most other humanoids.

fluffInfo.name: Feather Speech
fluffInfo.value: The ravenfolk have two languages: a verbal language full of croaks and whistles and a language of feathers. Ravenfolk can communicate volumes without speaking a word through the dyeing, arrangement, preening, and rustling of their plumage. This language is inherent to ravenfolk, and though others may use magic to understand it, it can't be used by creatures without feathers.

traits.name: Mimicry
traits.value: The ravenfolk scout can mimic animal sounds and Humanoid voices. A creature that hears the sounds can tell they are imitations with a successful DC 13 Wisdom (*Insight*) check.

traits.name: Writhing Aura
traits.value: The ground within 30 feet of the ravenous flora is filled with plant roots and becomes Difficult Terrain. A creature that starts its turn in the aura takes 7 (**2d6**) Poison damage.

traits.name: Poison Ivy
traits.value: If the ravenous flora would take Poison damage, it instead takes no damage and regains Hit Points equal to the Poison damage it would have received.

actions.name: The ravenous flora always takes its turn on Initiative count 20
actions.value: On its turn, the ravenous flora can use its movement and interaction as normal. However, it does not take an action or Bonus Action on its turn unless forced to do so by a spell or other effect. Instead, the ravenous flora takes one of the following Epic Actions at the end of each player character's turn:

entries: **Bite**: *Melee Attack Roll:* +7, reach 10 ft. *Hit:* 9 (**1d10 + 4**) Piercing damage, and the target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 15). Until this grapple ends, the target has the Restrained condition and the ravenous flora can't Bite another target.

**Spit Acid**: *Ranged Attack Roll:* +7, range 150/600 ft. *Hit:* 14 (**3d6 + 4**) Acid damage, and the target has the Burning condition (2d4 Acid). While Burning, the target has the Blinded condition.

**Swallow**: The ravenous flora makes one Bite attack against a Medium or smaller target it has Grappled. If the attack hits, the target is swallowed and the grapple ends. The swallowed target has the Blinded and Restrained conditions, has Total Cover from attacks and effects outside the flora, and takes 10 (**3d6**) Acid damage at the start of each of its turns. The flora can have up to four targets swallowed at a time.
If the flora takes 15 damage or more on a single turn from a creature inside it, it must succeed on a DC 16 Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate all swallowed creatures, which land with the Prone condition in unoccupied spaces within 10 feet of it. If the flora dies, a swallowed creature no longer has the Restrained condition and can escape from the corpse using 5 feet of movement, exiting with the Prone condition.

actions.name: Hypnotic Pollen (1/Round)
actions.value: *Wisdom Saving Throw:* DC 16, each creature in a 60-foot Emanation originating from the ravenous flora. *Failure:* 9 (**2d8**) Psychic damage, and the target has the Weakened condition (save ends). While Weakened, the target must spend all of its movement on each of its turns to move directly toward the ravenous flora. During this movement, the target ignores Difficult Terrain caused by the flora's Writhing Aura.

actions.name: Epic Resistance
actions.value: The ravenous flora chooses one condition, spell, or other effect currently affecting them and rolls 1d20. On an 11+, the effect ends on it. The ravenous flora can use this action even if it would otherwise be unable to take actions, its actions are being controlled by another creature, or if a spell or effect alters its game statistics.

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.value: The ghoul has Advantage on attack rolls against a creature if at least one of the ghoul's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition.

actions.name: Rancid Bite
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +5, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 6 (**1d6 + 3**) Piercing damage plus 10 (**3d6**) Poison damage.

bonusActions.name: Aggressive
bonusActions.value: The ghoul moves up to its Speed toward a Hostile creature it can see.

fluffInfo.value: *This vaguely humanoid-shaped plant boasts shimmering black and plum-colored leaves sprouting from from its head, back, and arms. The leaves are wickedly sharp and can be shaken loose to form deadly slashing clouds.*

fluffInfo.name: Roots in Shadow
fluffInfo.value: Razorleaves grow where the veil between the Shadow Realm and the Material Plane has thinned and darkness bleeds through into the soil. Their plant-like bodies are tinged with shadow magic but are as tangible as any other shrub or tree. Their roots are made of pure shadow and have a corrupting effect on other plants and animals around them.

fluffInfo.name: Letting the Light Out
fluffInfo.value: Mature razorleaves have a darkening effect on the area in which they live. Nonmagical sources of light are only half as effective in these plants' groves. There is a 50% chance that a portal to the Shadow Realm will appear wherever three or more razorleaves dwell. Sustained by the presence of the plants, the portal serves as a doorway between worlds.

traits.name: Dark Ground
traits.value: As an action, the razorleaf can dig its roots into the ground, securing itself in place and causing the area in a 20-foot radius around it to be shrouded in shadow. While rooted in this way, the razorleaf's speed becomes 0, it can't be knocked prone, and its attacks deal an extra 3 (**1d6**) necrotic damage. This area is difficult terrain and nonmagical sources of light are only half as effective while within it. Small and smaller beasts with Intelligence 3 or lower in the area lose their natural coloration and turn pale grey. These creatures are charmed by the razorleaf while within the area. Plants and trees inside the area turn an ashen color. The razorleaf can recall its roots and end this effect as a bonus action.

traits.name: Do Not Touch
traits.value: A creature that touches the razorleaf or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it takes 3 (**1d6**) slashing damage.

traits.name: Light Sensitivity
traits.value: While in bright light, the razorleaf has disadvantage on attack rolls, as well as on Wisdom (*Perception*) checks that rely on sight.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The razorleaf makes two lacerating leaves attacks.

actions.name: Lacerating Leaves
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +5 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. *Hit:* 12 (**3d6 + 2**) slashing damage.

actions.name: Shower of Razors (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: The razorleaf shakes loose a deadly shower of slicing leaves. Each creature within 10 feet of the razorleaf must make a DC 14 Dexterity saving throw, taking 21 (**6d6**) slashing damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

fluffInfo.name: (10+) Draining Rejuvenation.
fluffInfo.value: You are aware of the creature's Feed Bonus Action

fluffInfo.name: (15+) Anomalous Influence.
fluffInfo.value: You recognize the cyst's ability scores and saving throws.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: The Reality Cyst is less of a hunter than it is a disease. It feeds off the confusion of creatures trapped in its illusions. It mimics the bending realities of the Space Between Worlds and mirrors that into the minds of those who are close to it. After their target enters a trance, it drinks their mental energy and grows.

The Reality Cyst does only one thing: it feeds. It cannot move or defend itself well against attacks. It relies on creatures succumbing to its Unhinged Reality trait and devouring their minds. Once discovered, there is little the cyst can do to survive.

traits.value: The reality cyst emits a 120-foot Emanation of unhinged reality. A creature that starts its turn in the Emanation is subjected to the following effect. *Wisdom Saving Throw:* DC 15. *Failure:* The target has the Immobilized condition until it leaves the Emanation. While Immobilized, the target believes itself to be in an altered and confused environment of shifting forms, and can't see or hear anything else. The target does not perceive itself to be stationary, and instead believes it is walking through a bizarre landscape. It can take an action on its turn to repeat the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. If the creature succeeds on its save or the effect ends for it, it is immune to the reality cyst's Unhinged Reality for 24 hours.

traits.name: Unusual Nature
traits.value: The reality cyst doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

actions.name: Psychic Whip
actions.value: *Melee or Ranged Attack Roll:* +7, reach 5 ft. or range 120 ft. *Hit:* 19 (**4d6 + 5**) Psychic damage, and the target has the Dazed condition until the end of the reality cyst's next turn. The reality cyst can target a creature Immobilized by its Unhinged Reality with this attack even if the creature has Total Cover.

bonusActions.name: Feed
bonusActions.value: Each creature Immobilized by Unhinged Reality takes 10 (**3d6**) Psychic damage. The reality cyst regains Hit Points equal to the total damage dealt, and its Hit Point Maximum increases by the same amount.

fluffInfo.name: Constructs of Metal and Flesh.
fluffInfo.value: Despite their outward appearances, Reautomata are constructs, not undead: their organic components operate more like machines than mere flesh. Such is the composition of a Reautomata that they fight on despite grievous injury, unflinching even as they are dismembered. Stopping a Reautomata necessitates mangling its body past the point of physical operation. Reautomata are ultimately brutal and decisive combatants that fight without regard for their personal well-being.

fluffInfo.name: Created in Torment.
fluffInfo.value: Reautomata must be skillfully made by a master Reanimator using the finest components. It is essential the work begin on both a living and fully conscious individual. Typically, most apothecaries perform the work without anesthetic, instead opting to sever the vocal cords of their victims so as to not have their screams disturb the grim work involved. Limbs are removed and replaced, and metal is grafted into flesh and welded into the bone of the fully aware subject. Nervous tissue is pulled from the brain and distributed from the body, giving the construct nearly perfect proprioceptive awareness while excising unnecessary or superfluous brain tissues associated with cognitive functions. The process renders the Reautomata fully obedient, but not mindless.

fluffInfo.value: Characters proficient in *Arcana* or *Medicine* gain Advantage on Wisdom (*Insight*) or Intelligence (*Investigation*) checks to Study a Reautomata Each successful check reveals one of the following pieces of information:

fluffInfo.name: (16+) Dispassionate Metal and Flesh.
fluffInfo.value: You are aware of the Reautomata's Relentless Endurance trait, as well as its damage and condition Immunities.

fluffInfo.name: (19+) Limb Weapons.
fluffInfo.value: You know of the Reautomata's Arm Blades and Entrapping Rend attacks.

fluffInfo.name: (21+) Focused Killer.
fluffInfo.value: You learn the Reautomata's Wisdom, Intelligence, and Charisma saving throws.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: Reautomata fight with outward ferocity and aggressive attacks which belie the cold, unfeeling calculation at the core of each solider. In battle, Reautomata launch themselves towards their foes in great leaps, impaling their targets upon their rending arm blades. The rending blades flense into flesh and latch on like hooks, allowing the Reautomata to restrain their targets. They then use their great strength to rend apart their restrained victims.

Reautomata unquestionably obey the orders of their creator and will fight until destroyed without regard for their own bodies. However, even with only general instructions, Reautomata fight intelligently and know how to utilize the environment to their advantage, making use of their climb speeds and jumping ability to prioritize dangerous targets.

traits.value: The reautomata deals double damage to objects and structures.
