traits.name: Minion
traits.value: If the graywarper takes damage from an attack or as the result of a failed saving throw, their hit points are reduced to 0. If the graywarper takes damage from another effect, they die if the damage equals or exceeds their hit point maximum; otherwise they take no damage.

traits.name: Psionic Nexus
traits.value: When a non-minion voiceless talker within 30 feet of the graywarper uses telepathy or manifests a psionic power, they can do so as if they were in the graywarper's space.

actions.name: Phase Chant (Group Attack)
actions.value: *Melee or Ranged Power Attack:* +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft., one target. *Hit:* 4 psychic damage. If the target is a creature and if three or more graywarpers joined the attack, the target must make a Charisma saving throw. The DC for this saving throw is 11 plus the number of graywarpers who joined the attack. On a failed save, the target becomes phased until the end of their next turn. While phased, the creature is translucent and immaterial, and they deal half damage with weapon attacks and unarmed strikes.

entries: **HP**: Seven times their level (number of d8 Hit Dice equal to their level)
**Skills**: arcana +3 plus PB, deception +1 plus PB
**Languages**: Common, Deep Speech, Undercommon, telepathy 60 ft.

actions.name: Signature Attack (Psionic Pistol)
actions.value: *Ranged Weapon Attack:* +3 plus PB to hit, range 80/320 ft., one target. *Hit:* **1d10 plus PB** force damage. Beginning at 7th level, the operative can make this attack twice, instead of once, when they take the Attack action on their turn.

actions.name: 3rd Level: Phasing Charge (3/Day)
actions.value: When the operative hits a creature with a signature attack, they can attempt to teleport the target. The target must succeed on a DC 10 plus PB Wisdom saving throw or be teleported up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space on the ground that the operative can see.

actions.name: 5th Level: Telekinetic Repulsion (3/Day)
actions.value: As an action, the operative releases a powerful pulse of energy. Each enemy within 10 feet of the operative must make a DC 10 plus PB Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes **PBd6** force damage and is pushed up to 10 feet directly away from the operative. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't pushed.

actions.name: 7th Level: Memory Thief (3/Day; 4th-Order Power; Concentration)
actions.value: The operative psionically plunders the mind of a creature they can see within 30 feet of them. The target must make a DC 10 plus PB Intelligence saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes 22 (**4d10**) psychic damage, and for 1 minute, the target's proficiency bonus is cumulatively lowered by 1 and the infiltrator gains a cumulative +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls and to each feature's save DC. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage and doesn't have their proficiency bonus reduced.
A creature whose proficiency bonus drops to 0 can't form new thoughts or speak, and they have disadvantage on ability checks, attack rolls, and saving throws.

fluffInfo.value: *A dragon seemingly formed of the night sky has bright white stars for eyes. Lesser stars twinkle in the firmament of the dragon's body.*

fluffInfo.name: Children of the Stars
fluffInfo.value: Void dragons drift through the empty spaces beyond the boundaries of the mortal world and wander between the stars. They are aloof, mingling only with the otherworldly beings that live above and beyond the earth, including the incarnate forms of the stars themselves.

fluffInfo.name: Witnesses to the Void
fluffInfo.value: Void dragons are intensely knowledgeable creatures, but they have seen too much, lingering at the edge of the Void itself. They carry a piece of that nothing with them, and it flows out of them to break the minds of lesser beings when the dragons fly into a rage.

fluffInfo.name: Voracious Scholars
fluffInfo.value: Despite their removed existence and strange quirks, Void dragons still hoard treasure. Gems that glitter like the stars of their home are particularly prized. Their crowning piece, however, is knowledge. Void dragons jealously hoard scraps of forbidden and forgotten lore of any kind and spend most of their time at home poring over these treasures.

traits.name: Chill of the Void
traits.value: Creatures with resistance to cold damage don't have resistance to the cold damage dealt by the Void dragon. A creature with immunity to cold damage is still immune to the dragon's cold damage.

traits.name: Expert Void Traveler
traits.value: The Void dragon doesn't require air, food, drink, sleep, or ambient pressure. While traveling in the Void, the dragon magically glides on solar winds, covering immense distances in short times.

actions.name: Bite
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 8 (**1d10 + 3**) piercing damage plus 3 (**1d6**) cold damage.

actions.name: Breath Weapons (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: The dragon uses one of the following breath weapons.

entries: **Gravitic Breath**: The dragon exhales localized gravity in a 15‑foot cube, originating from the dragon. When a creature ends a fall in the cube, it takes **1d10** bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet it fell, to a maximum of 20d10. A creature that enters the cube for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, the creature is restrained. On a success, the creature's speed is halved as long as it remains in the cube. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. The cube lasts until the start of the dragon's next turn.

**Stellar Breath**: The dragon exhales star fire in a 15-foot cone. Each creature in that area must make a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw, taking 10 (**3d6**) fire damage and 10 (**3d6**) radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

fluffInfo.name: Stronger Together
fluffInfo.value: These altered survivors can no longer return to the Mortal World and need the chaotic contaminated environment to survive, but they are also regarded as foreign entities within the Space Between Worlds. Thus, many of the alien creatures inhabiting the twisted landscapes will attack, abduct, or obliterate them on sight.

These survivors have banded together into roving groups of scavengers, pirates, or gangs. They traverse the Void Sea upon scraped-together starships powered by elemental magics. These Void Pirates search and plunder the ancient ruins, caverns, and debris fields looking for anything that will help them survive. They wage war against alien entities and feed on the flesh of their kills, further inducing the never-ending descent into madness and contamination.

When they encounter mortals from another plane, Void Pirates are unpredictable. Sometimes they help lost sailors navigate the sea, hoping the dangerous voyage fails, and a new recruit can join their company. Other times, the pirates are less outwardly kind, kidnapping newcomers and holding them in cells upon their vessels. They use them as a distraction when they come across some horrible entity looking to eat, or as a bargaining chip amongst the other pirates, or even as payment to Far Dwellers for safe passage. A mortal life seems to be of value to many of the strange creatures, so having a few in reserve is often a key to survival.

fluffInfo.name: Ships of the Void Sea
fluffInfo.value: The vessels used by Void Pirates vary from group to group. They range from a small skiff with a sail and winged oars, housing a few pirates, to massive floating castles with elementally fueled propulsion systems housing hundreds.

Some void pirate ships resemble traditional pirate ships, while others appear as floating rafts with makeshift homes, or a series of roped together platforms drifting along. All these ships are bound together in a crude construction made up of junk and debris that has formed randomly in the Space Between Worlds or drifted into the void through Thin Places. Pirates hunt for better parts, or stronger materials to upgrade their vessels to defend against threats, or to exploit the other gangs of the sea.
Void Pirate ships are often equipped with extra nets, and sometimes ballistae or canons. Some even have more bizarre weaponry befitting the Space Between Worlds

fluffInfo.name: Myriad Forms of Chaos
fluffInfo.value: Void Pirates take on all manner of unusual quirks and physical attributes that represent their prolonged exposure to the shifting chaos of the Space Between Worlds.

fluffInfo.name: 1. No Face
fluffInfo.value: It has no face, only a smooth fleshy surface.

fluffInfo.name: 2. Eyes!
fluffInfo.value: Either not enough, or far too many, glow with an octarine haze.

fluffInfo.name: 3. Twinsies
fluffInfo.value: Two of these creatures are identical in every way.
They in fact are the same creature fractured in time.

fluffInfo.name: 4. Disjointed
fluffInfo.value: The creature's limbs have extra joints, or its joints bend the wrong way.

fluffInfo.name: 5. Cosmic Flesh
fluffInfo.value: The creature's flesh is a fractal distortion of light and energy.

fluffInfo.name: 6. Phasing
fluffInfo.value: The creature moves in and out of space, sometimes briefly appearing in two places at once as they walk around.

fluffInfo.name: 7. Impossible Dimensions
fluffInfo.value: The creature cannot be viewed from any perspective except straight on. Attempts to move around them fail as they seem to move with you, as if they are simply two-dimensional in a three-dimensional space.

fluffInfo.name: 8. Ventriloquist
fluffInfo.value: The sound of the creature's echoing voice seems to come from anywhere except their mouth.

fluffInfo.name: 9. Inside Out
fluffInfo.value: This creature appears to be inside out, their veins and organs exposed.

fluffInfo.name: 10. Insectoid
fluffInfo.value: This creature has taken on qualities of insects in their physical appearance, forming insect eyes, limbs, or mandibles.

fluffInfo.name: 11. Octarine Lamp
fluffInfo.value: This creature has a single eyeless socket, but instead of an eye, it emits a glowing octarine light.

fluffInfo.name: 12. Does this look infected?
fluffInfo.value: This creature is swollen and leaking puss and ooze from various open sores upon its body, at times bubbling or spurting with neon colored goop.

fluffInfo.name: Study the Foe
fluffInfo.value: Characters proficient in *History* or *Nature* gain Advantage on Intelligence (*Arcana*) checks when they take the Study action to examine a Void Pirate, learning the following based on the result.

fluffInfo.name: (5+) Mortal Survivors
fluffInfo.value: You learn the creature's type.

fluffInfo.name: (10+) Battle Readiness
fluffInfo.value: You recognize the creature's Bonus Action.

fluffInfo.name: (15+) Varied Abilities
fluffInfo.value: They learn the creature's highest and lowest ability scores.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: Void Pirates often attempt to abduct creatures rather than kill them. They fight without honor, aiming to quickly outnumber and out maneuver opponents. Many target threatening enemies with ship-mounted weapons, or they move in close to use nets and shackles to capture other humanoids. They nearly always take prisoners unless forced to kill a target. If a creature persistently attacks or breaks free, they may decide to slit their throat and use them as bait. They flee if risking defeat. Their lives are more valuable to them than prisoners or treasure.

fluffInfo.name: Harvestable Components
fluffInfo.value: Due to their humanoid origins, these creatures cannot be harvested.

traits.name: From Another World
traits.value: The void pirate doesn't have the standard Aberrant Traits other creatures in the Space Between Worlds have.

traits.name: Keen Eye, Sharp Wit
traits.value: The void pirate has Advantage on Initiative rolls.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The void pirate makes three attacks.

actions.name: Void Longsword
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +9, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 21 (**3d10 + 5**) Force damage.

actions.name: Pirate Pistol
actions.value: *Ranged Attack Roll:* +9, range 30/120 ft. *Hit:* 14 (**2d8 + 5**) Piercing damage.

bonusActions.name: Bark Orders
bonusActions.value: One void pirate squib or quartermaster within 60 feet of the void pirate can use its Reaction to move up to half its Speed or make an attack.

fluffInfo.name: Stronger Together
fluffInfo.value: These altered survivors can no longer return to the Mortal World and need the chaotic contaminated environment to survive, but they are also regarded as foreign entities within the Space Between Worlds. Thus, many of the alien creatures inhabiting the twisted landscapes will attack, abduct, or obliterate them on sight.

These survivors have banded together into roving groups of scavengers, pirates, or gangs. They traverse the Void Sea upon scraped-together starships powered by elemental magics. These Void Pirates search and plunder the ancient ruins, caverns, and debris fields looking for anything that will help them survive. They wage war against alien entities and feed on the flesh of their kills, further inducing the never-ending descent into madness and contamination.

When they encounter mortals from another plane, Void Pirates are unpredictable. Sometimes they help lost sailors navigate the sea, hoping the dangerous voyage fails, and a new recruit can join their company. Other times, the pirates are less outwardly kind, kidnapping newcomers and holding them in cells upon their vessels. They use them as a distraction when they come across some horrible entity looking to eat, or as a bargaining chip amongst the other pirates, or even as payment to Far Dwellers for safe passage. A mortal life seems to be of value to many of the strange creatures, so having a few in reserve is often a key to survival.

fluffInfo.name: Ships of the Void Sea
fluffInfo.value: The vessels used by Void Pirates vary from group to group. They range from a small skiff with a sail and winged oars, housing a few pirates, to massive floating castles with elementally fueled propulsion systems housing hundreds.

Some void pirate ships resemble traditional pirate ships, while others appear as floating rafts with makeshift homes, or a series of roped together platforms drifting along. All these ships are bound together in a crude construction made up of junk and debris that has formed randomly in the Space Between Worlds or drifted into the void through Thin Places. Pirates hunt for better parts, or stronger materials to upgrade their vessels to defend against threats, or to exploit the other gangs of the sea.
Void Pirate ships are often equipped with extra nets, and sometimes ballistae or canons. Some even have more bizarre weaponry befitting the Space Between Worlds

fluffInfo.name: Myriad Forms of Chaos
fluffInfo.value: Void Pirates take on all manner of unusual quirks and physical attributes that represent their prolonged exposure to the shifting chaos of the Space Between Worlds.

fluffInfo.name: 2. Eyes!

fluffInfo.name: 3. Twinsies
fluffInfo.value: Two of these creatures are identical in every way.
They in fact are the same creature fractured in time.

fluffInfo.name: 4. Disjointed
fluffInfo.value: The creature's limbs have extra joints, or its joints bend the wrong way.

fluffInfo.name: 5. Cosmic Flesh

fluffInfo.name: 6. Phasing
fluffInfo.value: The creature moves in and out of space, sometimes briefly appearing in two places at once as they walk around.

fluffInfo.name: 7. Impossible Dimensions
fluffInfo.value: The creature cannot be viewed from any perspective except straight on. Attempts to move around them fail as they seem to move with you, as if they are simply two-dimensional in a three-dimensional space.

fluffInfo.name: 8. Ventriloquist

fluffInfo.value: *Writhing black tendrils stretch from this indistinct orb of pure shadow. The faintest flicker of something green, like an eye, appears for a moment in the center of the globe and then fades to black again.*

fluffInfo.name: Called from Darkness
fluffInfo.value: Voidlings are creatures of the darkest part of the Void, the cold space between the stars. They are drawn to mortal realms by practitioners of foul, corrupting magic known to break the minds of those who wield it. They frequently are summoned servants to Void dragons, and they have been seen as wardens of the temples on the Plateau of Leng.

fluffInfo.name: Sustained by Darkness
fluffInfo.value: Voidlings are said to devour life and knowledge, and they subsist on darkness. The places they inhabit are known for their dank chill and obscurity. Voidlings are summoned by those hungry for power at any cost, and—despite their dark reputation—they serve well for years or even decades, until one day they turn on their summoners. If they slay their summoner, they grow in strength and return to the Void. Exactly what voidlings seek when they have not been summoned—and what triggers their betrayals—is a mystery.

fluffInfo.name: Cold Tendrils
fluffInfo.value: Creatures of utter darkness, they can barely be said to have a shape. They consist largely of lashing tendrils of solid shadow. The tendrils meet at a central point and form a rough sphere in which something like an eye appears intermittently. Though their tentacles stretch ten feet long, the core of a voiding is no more than four feet across, and it weighs nothing, darting through either air or Void with impressive speed.

traits.name: Darkness Regeneration
traits.value: While in an area of dim light or darkness, the voidling regains 5 hp at the start of its turn if it has at least 1 hp.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.value: The voidling has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Void Traveler
traits.value: The voidling doesn't require air, food, drink, sleep, or ambient pressure.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The voidling makes four Shadow Tendril or Necrotic Bolt attacks. If two Necrotic Bolt attacks hit one creature, the target must succeed on a DC 17 Wisdom saving throw or be frightened until the end of its next turn.

actions.name: Shadow Tendril
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +9 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. *Hit:* 8 (**1d6 + 5**) bludgeoning damage plus 10 (**3d6**) necrotic damage.

actions.name: Necrotic Bolt
actions.value: *Ranged Spell Attack:* +7 to hit, range 120 ft., one target. *Hit:* 17 (**4d6 + 3**) necrotic damage.

actions.name: Shadow's Grasp (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: The voidling releases a wave of small, grasping tendrils of shadow. Each creature within 20 feet of it must make a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, a creature takes 49 (**14d6**) necrotic damage and is restrained by tendrils of shadow for 1 minute. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn't restrained. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

fluffInfo.value: *What at first appears to be a humanoid wearing voluminous robes is a thin, fiendish figure whose skin drapes about its form like a wet shroud.*

These minor fiends are often found in the service of more powerful fiends or, occasionally, powerful mortals. Volguloths are quiet, efficient killers and often act as assassins. They are sadistic and cruel, reveling in the deaths they cause, and are loathe to turn their stealthy skills to less violent tasks, such as theft or reconnaissance.

fluffInfo.name: Skin Shroud
fluffInfo.value: A volguloth's skin behaves more like a sinuous sheet of muscle, contracting and expanding as the volguloth requires. Typically, it drapes the fiend's form like a robe. However, the volguloth can tighten it to a rumpled but close-fitting hide or extend it into long sheets. This allows it to glide short distances or enwrap and smother victims, engulfing them in the folds of its skin and squeezing them until they run out of air.

entries: **Resistances**: cold, fire, lightning; bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from nonmagical attacks

traits.name: Glide
traits.value: The volguloth has draping skin that it can expand while falling to slow its rate of descent to 60 feet per round, landing on its feet and taking no falling damage. It can move up to 5 feet horizontally for every 1 foot it falls. The volguloth can't gain height with its expanded skin alone. If subjected to a strong wind or lift of any kind, it can use the updraft to glide farther.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.value: The volguloth has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Poisoned Weapons
traits.value: The volguloth's weapons are coated with a magical poison. When the volguloth hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra **2d6** poison damage (included in the attack).

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The volguloth makes two Claw attacks. If both Claw attacks hit a Medium or smaller target, the target is grappled (escape DC 13), and the volguloth uses its Enshroud on the target.

actions.name: Claw
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 8 (**2d4 + 3**) slashing damage plus 7 (**2d6**) poison damage.

actions.name: Enshroud
actions.value: The volguloth enshrouds a Medium or smaller target grappled by it. The enshrouded target is blinded, restrained, and unable to breathe or speak until the grapple ends. If the volguloth moves, the enshrouded target moves with it. The volguloth can have only one creature enshrouded at a time, and it can't use its Glide trait while enshrouding a creature.

bonusActions.name: Strangle
bonusActions.value: A creature enshrouded by the volguloth must succeed on a DC 13 Strength saving throw or take 10 (**3d6**) bludgeoning damage and begin suffocating, as the air is squeezed from its lungs.

traits.name: Training
traits.value: The commoner has proficiency in one skill of the DM's choice and has Advantage whenever it makes an ability check using that skill.

actions.name: Club
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +2, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 2 (**1d4**) Bludgeoning damage.

fluffInfo.name: Constricted Origins
fluffInfo.value: Once a realm of humanoids who worshiped serpents, the ancient Vos'skyriss Empire was among the richest in the world. Its people obsessively imitated snakes—their flexibility, their emotionless patience, their willingness to survive at any costs (even cannibalizing their own kind), and their cold detachment. With the help of profane magics, most of the Vos'skyriss shed the useless skin of their humanity to become like the Betrayer God known as the __The Cloaked Serpent__. Those who couldn't evolve became food for those who did.

Seers of the Vos'skyriss foresaw the Calamity, and the empire created an arcane stasis field under their capital city of Vos'skyriss to survive. This site stands off the western coast of Tal'Dorei and is now known as Visa Isle. Only the strongest were allowed to seek refuge in the capital, and decades of carefully tracked tournaments determined who was fit for survival.

fluffInfo.name: Ophidian Society
fluffInfo.value: Serpentfolk occupy remote temples in jungles, swamps, and deserts. Their society enforces strict discipline and a hierarchy that rewards those closest to snakes in mind and body. Serpentfolk transfigured into massive snakes with humanoid arms are held in the highest esteem.
Despite their god's moniker, the Vos'skyriss serpentfolk outlaw hoods so that outsiders in their realm are easily recognizable.

fluffInfo.name: Narcissistic Worship
fluffInfo.value: Most serpentfolk have little love for the __The Cloaked Serpent__, though they pay him homage as the deity of poisons, assassins, and darkness. For the Vos'skyriss serpentfolk, worship is a means to an end. Their legends say that the devout will be granted the ability to devour nightmares, enabling them to gorge themselves on dreams of fear and terror until they grow so large that they can turn on their god and swallow the __The Cloaked Serpent__ himself. Once begun, this feast is unending—they will devour the remaining gods one by one, and finally, the entirety of the multiverse.

fluffInfo.name: Vos'skyriss Rising
fluffInfo.value: Several decades ago, Jorlund Vohr, professor of archaeology at the Alabaster Lyceum, led an expedition to the ruins upon Visa Isle—and found them prowled by the restless spirits of the serpent empire. Their incursion unleashed these entombed spirits, and awakened hundreds of their living kin from magical stasis. Now, living and undead serpentfolk plot together to rekindle the embers of their long-lost empire.

traits.name: Ethereal Sight
traits.value: The ghost can see 60 feet into the Ethereal Plane when it is on the Material Plane, and vice versa.

traits.name: Incorporeal Movement
traits.value: The ghost can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 5 (**1d10**) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The ghost makes two spear attacks.

actions.name: Spear
actions.value: *Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack:* +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. *Hit:* 6 (**1d6 + 3**) piercing damage plus 7 (**2d6**) necrotic damage. If the ghost makes a ranged attack, its spear rematerializes in its hands after the attack is resolved.

actions.name: Etherealness
actions.value: The ghost enters the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane, or vice versa. It is visible on the Material Plane while it is in the Border Ethereal, and vice versa, yet it can't affect or be affected by anything on the other plane.

actions.name: Terrifying Hiss
actions.value: The ghost emits an uncanny, rasping hiss. Each non-undead creature within 30 feet of the ghost that can hear it must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throws or be frightened for 1 minute. A frightened target can repeat the saving throws at the end of each of its turns, ending the condition on itself on a success. If a target's saving throws is successful or the effect ends for it, the target is immune to this ghost's Terrifying Hiss for the next 24 hours.

fluffInfo.value: This is the stat block of the __berserker__, adjusted with vulpin traits.

traits.name: Evasive
traits.value: The berserker adds its Intelligence modifier as a bonus to its Dexterity saving throws (already included in the stat block).

traits.name: Reckless

fluffInfo.value: Contaminated Elementals can be found all over Drakkenheim, often in areas where the eldritch magics are especially concentrated. Many who have encountered these elementals have spoken of the city itself coming to life to attack them. Reports of ruins reaching out and crushing adventurers, burning flames moving and hunting with minds of their own, or contaminated pools lurching to engulf passersby have been heard. Even the blowing air itself has mustered parts of the Haze into shifting clouds that stalk adventurers through the streets. These magical creatures are a constant reminder that nothing in the city can be trusted, and that nowhere is truly safe.

traits.name: Death Burst

Each creature within 30 feet of it must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or take 42 (**12d6**) necrotic damage and gain one level of contamination (DungeonsDrakkenheim). In addition, this explosion triggers a random arcane anomaly (see Dungeons of Drakkenheim).

fluffInfo.value: True to its name and nature, characters may be able to collect delerium from the remains of the Walking Delerium Geode, though its destruction tends to cause many crystals to shatter and break.

Roll 1d20 to determine what the characters can find: 1—nothing remains but broken splinters and ash; 2–9: 4d6 delerium chips; 10–12: 3d10 delerium fragments; 13–16: 2d6 delerium shards; 17–19: 1d4 delerium crystals; 20: 1 delerium geode.

fluffInfo.value: Wall Gargoyles are found only along the city walls. They animate and attack characters who dare attempt any of the following: Climbing more than halfway up the walls or towers, flying within one hundred fifty feet of the city walls horizontally, or over them at any height, or lingering on the walls or towers for more than ten minutes.

The gargoyles attack directly, viciously, and without remorse. If they reduce their quarry to 0 Hit Points, they spend their next turn tearing apart the creature's body before moving on to another target. The gargoyles pursue their quarry into the city to any distance until they or their quarry are destroyed, but give up pursuing characters more than three hundred feet outside the city walls.

fluffInfo.value: *A raven-haired young woman rises to the surface of the water as she swims, singing softly to herself. Her lower body is revealed to be that of a mountain lion, and her sweet song suddenly turns to a yowl of rage.*
Wampus cats are all born from an ancient shaman's curse. Trollkin, orc, goblin, and human shamans alike all claim to be able to transform those who practice forbidden magic into wampus cats.

fluffInfo.name: Forest Streams
fluffInfo.value: The wampus cat stalks the shores of woodland waterways, using her magic to disguise her true form and lure unsuspecting victims to the water's edge. She is particularly fond of attacking bathers or those pulling water from a stream.

fluffInfo.name: Hatred of the Holy
fluffInfo.value: While she prefers to feast on intelligent male humanoids, she holds special animosity toward holy men of any kind. Unless near starvation or if provoked, however, she will not kill women. Indeed, a wampus cat may strike up a temporary friendship with any woman who is having difficulties with men, though these friendships typically last only as long as their mutual enemies live. Some witches are said to gain their trust and keep them as companions.

fluffInfo.name: Swamp Team Ups
fluffInfo.value: Will-o'-wisps and miremals enjoy working in tandem with wampus cats; the wisps alter their light to mimic the flicker of a torch or candle and illuminate the disguised cat, the better to lure in victims, then assist the cat in the ensuing battle. Miremals use a tall story to lure travelers into a swamp when the hour grows late, then abandon them.

traits.name: Divine Animosity
traits.value: The wampus cat has advantage on attack rolls against creatures wielding divine or celestial power, such as clerics, paladins, or aasimars.

actions.value: The wampus cat sings a sweet melody. Each creature within 60 feet of her that can hear the song must succeed on a DC 13 Charisma saving throw or be charmed for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If a creature's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is immune to the wampus cat's Sweet Song for the next 24 hours.

actions.name: Terrifying Yowl (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: The wampus cat emits an ear‑piercing yowl. Each creature within 15 feet of the wampus cat that can hear the yowl must make a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, a creature takes 10 (**3d6**) thunder damage and is frightened until the end of its next turn. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn't frightened.

bonusActions.name: Change Shape

fluffInfo.value: *A beautifully manicured garden pond sits before you, complete with a white marble bench. The surface of its crystal‑blue water ripples gently, which seems odd, because there is no wind.*
Wandering ponds are a curious variety of ooze that possess a modicum of fey magic.

fluffInfo.name: Fairy Made
fluffInfo.value: Wandering ponds are suspected of having originated in the fey realms where schemes to trap and humiliate wanderers are widespread pastimes. Certainly, the pond's unique ability to weave a glamour over itself indicates these creatures are no ordinary ooze.

fluffInfo.name: Mysterious Motives
fluffInfo.value: Wandering ponds always operate in the same way. A pond disguises itself to attract prey and then pulls them in. Once unconscious, the victim is teleported to a random body of water within the area. It is unclear what benefit the pond receives from such a scheme, but it is regarded as further evidence of fey involvement.

traits.name: Dowsing Sense
traits.value: The wandering pond instinctively knows the direction, size, and location of all bodies of water containing at least 30 gallons of liquid within 1 mile of its location.

traits.name: Faerie Glamour
traits.value: While the wandering pond remains motionless, it is covered in an illusory glamour that makes it appear like a charming pond. The pond seems completely real, including sounds and smells appropriate to the depicted pond. Physical interaction with the pond reveals its nature, and the creatures who can see through illusion perceive the ooze for what it really is.

An engulfed creature is blinded and restrained, it has total cover against attacks and other effects outside the pond, and it takes 10 (**3d6**) acid damage at the start of each of the wandering pond's turns. A creature reduced to 0 hit points in this way becomes stable and is instantly teleported to a random body of water within 1 mile of the wandering pond.

The wandering pond can only have one creature swallowed at a time. While the pond isn't incapacitated, it can regurgitate the creature at any time (no action required) in a space within 5 feet of it. The creature exits prone. If the wandering pond dies, it likewise regurgitates a swallowed creature.

bonusActions.value: The war chaplain commands an ally within 30 feet. The target can use its Reaction to make one attack against a creature the chaplain attacked this round.

fluffInfo.value: *The large, flightless bird dove in and out of battle, screeching defiantly as its rider drove a spear into its foes.*

In the wild, war ostriches are dangerous and skittish, prone to lashing out with punishing kicks while sprinting around the battlefield. Humanoids in grasslands use them to create chaos by driving a flock of fast-moving war ostriches into a caravan or enemy troop formations.

*War ostriches are commonly found throughout the Southlands both as wild and domestic animals. The people of Nuria Natal, in particular, use war ostriches as beasts of burden and mounts along the River Nuria, switching to camels for long treks across the Crescent or Sarklan Deserts. Further south, gnolls and nkosi both hunt and domesticate war ostriches, and many warriors decorate their armor, clothing, or hair with the feathers of favored mounts who helped the warrior achieve greatness in battle.*

fluffInfo.name: Faster than Horses
fluffInfo.value: War ostriches have been domesticated for centuries. They are a fearsome sight on the field of combat when bearing warriors into battle. War ostriches are heavily employed in regions where horses are rare or impractical or where their leaping ability enables cavalry to charge over broken ground. Stubborn and willful, these creatures are difficult to train. Once trained though, they are loyal and fierce mounts, fighting to the death in battle alongside their riders.

traits.name: Leaping Pounce
traits.value: If the war ostrich jumps at least 15 feet straight toward a creature and then hits it with a Claw attack on the same turn, that target must succeed on a DC 13 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone. If the target is prone, the ostrich can make one Beak attack against it as a bonus action.

traits.name: Standing Leap
traits.value: The war ostrich's long jump is up to 30 feet and its high jump is up to 15 feet, with or without a running start.

actions.name: Beak

actions.name: Intimidating Screech
actions.value: The war ostrich screeches at a creature it can see within 30 feet of it. The target must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or have disadvantage on attack rolls until the end of its next turn, as the screech rattles it.

bonusActions.name: Skittish
bonusActions.value: The war ostrich takes the Dash or Disengage action.

traits.name: Baby Burst
traits.value: When the spider dies, a __swarm of spiders__ bursts forth from their remains and acts on the same initiative count as the spider did.

traits.name: Rider Launcher
traits.value: An allied rider who jumps off the spider has a long jump of 30 feet and a high jump of 15 feet, with or without a running start. If an allied rider jumps off the spider, the first melee weapon attack the ally makes on the same turn has advantage.

traits.name: Spider Climb

traits.name: Web Walker

fluffInfo.value: *Once we have all the shiny, the Rat God will come and help us! We'll get food! We will eat! Lots of food! All the food! We will eat the whole world! All the earth! Yes yes yes!*

Many ratlings worship a fiendish entity they call the Rat God. They construct crude effigies to the Rat God, who whispers to the most cunning and intelligent ratlings, granting them magic through eldritch pacts. Ratlings understand surprisingly little about the Rat God, and make up stories and fables about the Rat God's exploits.

traits.name: Skulker
traits.value: The ratling can take the Hide action as a bonus action on each of its turns.

traits.name: Keen Smell
traits.value: The ratling has advantage on Wisdom (*Perception*) checks that rely on smell.

actions.name: Bite
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 4 (**1d4 + 2**) piercing damage.

fluffInfo.name: (5+) Otherworldly Pact
fluffInfo.value: You are aware these creatures have an excellent sense of smell, Darkvision, are capable climbers and swimmers and this ratling's damage Resistances.

fluffInfo.name: (10+) Potent Spellcasting
fluffInfo.value: You learn of the ratling's Balefire and Conjure Swarms actions.

fluffInfo.name: (15+) Commanding but Frail
fluffInfo.value: You know the ratling's strongest and weakest ability scores and saving throws.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: A Warlock of the Rat God does everything in its power to put "lesser" ratlings between it and its enemies. They deem themselves far too valuable to be put in harm's way, but are also inherently overconfident in their powers, convinced the Rat God protects them from harm.

A Warlock of the Rat God will have likely cast __Mage Armor__ on itself prior to rolling Initiative, as most keep this spell active when venturing out of their burrow, or at the first sign of danger. They conjure a Swarm of Rats to pester their enemies, and use Balefire to pummel their foes. When their defenses are exhausted they cast __Invisibility__ on themselves and attempt to flee using __Teleport__.

fluffInfo.value: Characters proficient in *History* or *Nature* gain Advantage on Intelligence (*Arcana*) checks when they take the Study action to examine a Warp Marauder, learning the following based on the result.

fluffInfo.name: (10+) Mentally Tough
fluffInfo.value: You learn the creature's Resistances and Immunities.

fluffInfo.name: (15+) Reality Distortion
fluffInfo.value: You are aware of the creature's Swirling Color Field trait.

fluffInfo.name: (20+) Strong and Nimble
fluffInfo.value: You know the creature's highest and lowest ability scores.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: The Warp Marauder has control over the reality around it. It grabs creatures and drags them into extraplanar realities where it feeds on them. The lupine alien isn't afraid to be hit, relying on its ability to alter time and space from an incoming attack, directing an essence of chaotic circumstance back towards the creature.
Warp Marauders flee if they are reduced below half their Hit Points.

traits.name: Fully Contaminated
traits.value: The warp marauder is immune to Contamination and has Advantage on saving throws against contaminated spells. The warp marauder may cast contaminated spells even though it does not gain Contamination levels.

traits.name: Delerium Healing
traits.value: As an action, the warp marauder can touch a delerium shard to regain 10 (3d6) Hit Points. Once the warp marauder has used a delerium shard in this way, the shard can't be used in this manner again for 24 hours.

traits.name: Alien Intellect
traits.value: The warp marauder is immune to any effect that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts, as well as any divination spell that it refuses. Wisdom (*Insight*) checks made to ascertain the warp marauder's intentions or sincerity have Disadvantage.

traits.name: Extraplanar Gullet
traits.value: The warp marauder's back opens into a large mouth that leads to an extradimensional gullet. Anything it swallows is transported into this extraplanar space, which manifests as a rhizomatic network of slurping tunnels and fleshy passages. This space can hold any number of creatures of any size, and nothing inside the space can harm the warp marauder.

A creature within the gullet can take an action to attempt to escape, making a DC 15 Intelligence saving throw. On a success, it reappears in the nearest unoccupied space within 5 feet of the warp marauder. On a failure, it takes 10 (**3d6**) Psychic damage. If the warp marauder dies, everything inside the extraplanar gullet appears in the nearest unoccupied spaces to its corpse.

traits.name: Grasping Tentacles
traits.value: The warp marauder can have up to four tentacles at a time. Each tentacle has AC 20, 10 Hit Points, and Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. Destroying a tentacle deals no damage to the warp marauder, which can extrude a replacement tentacle on its next turn. A creature within 5 feet can take an action to break a tentacle with a successful DC 15 Strength check.

traits.name: Swirling Color Field
traits.value: A field of shimmering color reverberates around the warp marauder, distorting reality. A creature that hits the warp marauder with an attack suffers one of the following effects, determined randomly (roll 1d6). A creature Grappled and adjacent to the warp marauder isn't affected by the Swirling Color Field.

traits.name: 1-2: Blue
traits.value: The attacker is teleported to an unoccupied space the warp marauder can see within 20 feet. The chosen space must be on a surface or in a liquid that can support the target. The attacker is then subjected to the following effect. *Charisma Saving Throw:* DC 15. *Failure:* The target has the Immobilized condition (save ends).

traits.name: 3-4: Yellow
traits.value: *Dexterity Saving Throw:* DC 15. *Failure:* 21 (**6d6**) Lightning damage. *Success* Half damage.

traits.name: 5-6: Red
traits.value: *Wisdom Saving Throw:* DC 15. *Failure:* The target has the Staggered condition (save ends).

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The warp marauder makes four Tentacle attacks, uses Reel, and makes one Bite attack.

actions.name: Tentacle
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +7, reach 60 ft. *Hit:* The target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 15). While Grappled, the target has the Restrained condition and has Disadvantage on Strength checks and saving throws, and the warp marauder can't use this tentacle against another target.

actions.name: Bite
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +7, reach 5 ft, one creature Grappled by the warp marauder. *Hit:* 16 (**2d10 + 5**) Piercing damage, and the warp marauder swallows the target. The target, along with everything it is wearing and carrying, appears in the warp marauder's Extraplanar Gullet.

actions.name: Reel
actions.value: The warp marauder pulls each creature Grappled by it up to 30 feet straight toward it.

bonusActions.name: Dimensional Jump
bonusActions.value: The warp marauder teleports to an unoccupied space within 120 feet. Alternatively, it travels from the Material Plane to the Space Between Worlds or vice versa.

fluffInfo.value: These ethereal phantoms haunt the places where they died, grasping for any memory of their former identities. Their mental anguish breaks the minds of those who hear their wails, and they induce rapid mutations when they possess humanoid bodies.

traits.name: Incorporeal Movement

actions.name: Etherealness
actions.value: The ghost enters the Ethereal Plane from the Material Plane, or vice versa. It is visible on the Material Plane while it is in the Border Ethereal, and vice versa, yet it can't affect or be affected by anything on the other plane.

actions.name: Psychic Wail (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: Every creature within 30 feet of the warp witch must succeed on a DC 13 Intelligence saving throw or take 10 (**3d6**) psychic damage and become incapacitated until the end of the warp witches next turn.

actions.name: Mutate Host
actions.value: The warp witch can use a bonus action while it is possessing a creature to force mutations upon its host. The possessed creature must succeed on a DC 13 Charisma saving throw or gain one level of contamination (DungeonsDrakkenheim). Rather than rolling to determine if a mutation occurs, the warp witch automatically causes a random mutation.

actions.name: Possession (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: One humanoid that the ghost can see within 5 feet of it must succeed on a DC 13 Charisma saving throw or be possessed by the ghost; the ghost then disappears, and the target is incapacitated and loses control of its body. The ghost now controls the body but doesn't deprive the target of awareness. The ghost can't be targeted by any attack, spell, or other effect, except ones that turn undead, and it retains its alignment, Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, and immunity to being charmed and frightened. It otherwise uses the possessed target's statistics, but doesn't gain access to the target's knowledge, class features, or proficiencies.

The possession lasts until the body drops to 0 hit points, the ghost ends it as a bonus action, or the ghost is turned or forced out by an effect like the __dispel evil and good__ spell. When the possession ends, the ghost reappears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the body. The target is immune to this ghost's Possession for 24 hours after succeeding on the saving throw or after the possession ends.

fluffInfo.name: Study the Foe
fluffInfo.value: Characters proficient in *Arcana* gain Advantage on Intelligence (*Religion*) checks to Study a Warp Witch, learning the following based on their result:

fluffInfo.name: (5+) Resistant Undead
fluffInfo.value: You learn of the Warp Witch's Resistances and Immunities.

fluffInfo.name: (10+) Mutative Control
fluffInfo.value: You recongize the creature's Possession action and Mutate Host Bonus Action, but not the means to end the possession.

fluffInfo.name: (15+) Escaping Possession
fluffInfo.value: You are aware that the Warp Witch's Possession can be ended by reducing the possessed body to 0 Hit Points, or by casting __Dispel Evil and Good__.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: A Warp Witch begins combat by using its Psychic Scream. The witch then selects a target amongst their foes to possess.

While possessing a host, the Warp Witch will try to use the body to deceive or trick allies of its host into not attacking or harming them, trying to suggest useless, ineffective, and halfmad courses of action to "help" the host "drive out" the spirit, such whistling, dancing, clapping, singing, drawing pictures, and other bizarre commands. Meanwhile, the witch continues to use Mutate Host to contaminate them. The Warp Witch leaves the host after they undergo a Monstrous Transformation, and then moves to repeat the process with another.

traits.value: When the priest dies, each ally within 20 feet who can see the priest gains 10 Temporary Hit Points and a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls for 1 minute.

traits.name: Zealous Aura
traits.value: The priest radiates an aura of zeal in a 20-foot Emanation originating from it. Each ally in the area has Advantage on Initiative checks, and their successful attacks deal an extra **1d4** Radiant damage. This aura becomes inactive if the priest has the Incapacitated condition.

actions.name: Multiattack

actions.value: *Melee or Ranged Attack Roll:* +5 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 60 ft., one target. *Hit:* 7 (**2d6**) Radiant damage, and one ally of the priest within 20 feet of the target can take a Reaction to make a melee attack.

bonusActions.name: Righteous Morale (1/Day)
bonusActions.value: The priest chooses up to three other creatures it can see within 20 feet of it. Each target regains 4 (**1d8**) Hit Points and has Immunity to the Charmed and Frightened conditions until the start of the priest's next turn.

traits.name: False Appearance
traits.value: If the Watchwood Tree is motionless at the start of combat, it has advantage on its initiative roll. Moreover, if a creature hasn't observed the Watchwood Tree move or act, that creature must succeed on a DC 18 Intelligence (*Investigation*) check to discern that the Watchwood Tree isn't an ordinary tree.

traits.name: Unruly Earth
traits.value: The ground within a 15-foot radius centered on the Watchwood Tree is considered difficult terrain for all creatures besides the Watchwood Tree.

actions.name: Root Slam
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +4 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. *Hit:* 9 (**2d6 + 2**) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Watching Eye (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: The terrifying gaze of a Watchwood Tree can leave a creature frozen in its tracks. Each creature of the Watchwood Tree's choice within a 15-foot cone must succeed on a DC 12 Wisdom saving throw or become restrained; a creature that can't be frightened automatically succeeds on its saving throw. The Watchwood Tree can then immediately make a Root Slam attack against each creature that failed its saving throw.
A creature restrained in this way can use its action to make a DC 12 Wisdom check, freeing itself on a success.

traits.name: Water Form
traits.value: The elemental can enter a hostile creature's space and stop there. It can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing.

traits.name: Freeze
traits.value: If the elemental takes cold damage, it partially freezes; its speed is reduced by 20 feet until the end of its next turn.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The elemental makes two slam attacks.

actions.name: Slam
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 13 (**2d8 + 4**) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Whelm (Recharge 4-6)
actions.value: Each creature in the elemental's space must make a DC 15 Strength saving throw. On a failure, a target takes 13 (**2d8 + 4**) bludgeoning damage. If it is Large or smaller, it is also grappled (escape DC 14). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained and unable to breathe unless it can breathe water. If the saving throw is successful, the target is pushed out of the elemental's space.

The elemental can grapple one Large creature or up to two Medium or smaller creatures at one time. At the start of each of the elemental's turns, each target grappled by it takes 13 (**2d8 + 4**) bludgeoning damage. A creature within 5 feet of the elemental can pull a creature or object out of it by taking an action to make a DC 14 Strength check and succeeding.

fluffInfo.value: *The frog-headed, legless creature with wide, batlike wings opens its gaping maw and shrieks. Its long, sinuous tail whips around it, tipped in a barb dripping with poison.*

fluffInfo.name: Gliding Wings
fluffInfo.value: The creature has no legs or arms, but it sports a pair of wide, membranous wings. It uses its wings to glide beneath the water and to soar through the air.

fluffInfo.name: Scourge of Waterways
fluffInfo.value: Water leapers plague fresh lakes and rivers. They prey on animals that come to the water's edge to drink, as well as on fishermen that ply their trade in the water leaper's territory. Stories circulate among fishers of waterways known for broken lines and missing bait. Fishers give these areas a wide berth for fear of water leapers. Desperate or unwary fishers who ignore the warnings are never seen again; drifting, empty boats are the signs of their passing.

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.value: The water leaper can breathe air and water.

traits.name: Underwater Camouflage
traits.value: The water leaper has advantage on Dexterity (*Stealth*) checks made while underwater.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The water leaper makes one Bite attack and one Stinger attack.

actions.name: Bite
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 10 (**2d6 + 3**) piercing damage, and the target is grappled (escape DC 13). Until this grapple ends, the target is restrained, and the water leaper can't Bite another target.

actions.name: Stinger
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 12 (**2d8 + 3**) piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 1 minute. While poisoned in this way, the creature takes 5 (**2d4**) poison damage at the start of each of its turns. A poisoned creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

actions.name: Swallow
actions.value: The water leaper makes a Bite attack against a Medium or smaller creature it is grappling. If the attack hits, the target is also swallowed, and the grapple ends. While swallowed, the target is blinded and restrained, it has Cover against attacks and other effects outside the water leaper, and it takes 7 (**2d6**) acid damage at the start of each of the water leaper's turns. The water leaper can have only one creature swallowed at a time.

If the water leaper takes 15 damage or more on a single turn from the swallowed creature, the leaper must succeed on a DC 12 Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate the creature, which falls prone in a space within 5 feet of the leaper. If the leaper dies, a swallowed creature is no longer restrained by it and can escape from the corpse by using 10 feet of movement, exiting prone.

traits.name: Minion
traits.value: If the spark takes damage from an attack or as the result of a failed saving throw, their hit points are reduced to 0. If the spark takes damage from another effect, they die if the damage equals or exceeds their hit point maximum; otherwise they take no damage.

traits.name: Whirlpool Suction
traits.value: If an enemy starts their turn within 5 feet of three or more water sparks, the enemy must succeed on a Strength saving throw or have their speed reduced to 0. The DC for this saving throw equals 14 plus the number of water sparks within 5 feet of the enemy.

actions.name: Whelming Wave (Group Attack)
actions.value: *Melee or Ranged Spell Attack:* +11 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30 ft., one target. *Hit:* 10 bludgeoning damage, and if the attack was made by more than one spark, the target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be knocked prone and be unable to stand up until the end of the sparks' next turn. The DC for this saving throw equals 14 plus the number of sparks who joined the attack.

traits.name: Whirlpool Suction
traits.value: If an enemy starts their turn within 5 feet of three or more water sparks, the enemy must succeed on a Strength saving throw or have their speed reduced to 0. The DC for this saving throw equals 14 plus the number of water sparks within 5 feet of the enemy.

actions.name: Whelming Wave (Group Attack)
actions.value: *Melee or Ranged Spell Attack:* +11 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30 ft., one target. *Hit:* 10 bludgeoning damage, and if the attack was made by more than one spark, the target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be knocked prone and be unable to stand up until the end of the sparks' next turn. The DC for this saving throw equals 14 plus the number of sparks who joined the attack.

fluffInfo.value: *Lost Soul Bound to Regret*

fluffInfo.name: Secret
fluffInfo.value: Wayward haints can be trapped in empty bottles if they're tricked or forced to pass over one.

entries: **Resistances**: acid, bludgeoning, cold, fire, lightning, piercing, slashing, thunder
**Immunities**: poison; charmed, exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained

traits.name: Bottle Trap
traits.value: A haint that enters the space of an upright, empty bottle must succeed on a DC 16 Charisma saving throw or be drawn into the bottle, and a cork or stopper appears to close the bottle. The trapped haint can see and hear through the bottle out to 10 feet, and any creature in that range can hear the haint. The haint is released if the bottle breaks or another creature opens it.

traits.name: Incorporeal Movement
traits.value: The haint can move through other creatures and objects as if they were Difficult Terrain. It takes 5 (**1d10**) Force damage if it ends its turn inside a solid object.

actions.name: Draining Regret
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +4, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 10 (**3d6**) Psychic damage, and the target gains 1 Exhaustion level. This can't raise the target's Exhaustion level above 5, and all Exhaustion levels gained from this action end when the target finishes a Short or Long Rest, or if it receives a __Lesser Restoration__ spell or similar magic.

fluffInfo.value: *Hag of Soul Twisting and Terror*

fluffInfo.name: Secret
fluffInfo.value: Weasel hags' love of teeth goes beyond a mere quirk. They can't refuse a tooth willingly given by its owner and can't harm the owner for a time.

traits.name: Biting Gift
traits.value: If a creature willingly offers one of its teeth to the hag, the hag must accept it and has the Charmed condition for 24 hours, or until the creature or its allies deal damage to the hag or force it to make a saving throw.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.value: The hag has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The hag makes one Bite attack and uses Spellcasting (at will spells only).

actions.name: Bite
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +6, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 8 (**1d8 + 4**) Piercing damage plus 10 (**3d6**) Psychic damage.

actions.name: Waking Terrors (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: *Wisdom Saving Throw:* DC 13, one creature the hag can see within 30 feet. If the hag has one of the target's teeth, the target has Disadvantage on the save. *Failure:* 21 (**6d6**) Psychic damage, and the target has the Frightened condition.

While Frightened in this way, the target perceives its allies as enemies born from its nightmares, but it isn't compelled to act against or harm them. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically. *Success* Half damage only.

bonusActions.name: Shape-Shift
bonusActions.value: The hag shape-shifts to resemble a Tiny __weasel__ (Speed 30 ft., Climb 30 ft.) or a Small or Medium Humanoid, or back into her true form. Her game statistics, other than her Speed as a weasel and her size, are the same in each form. Any equipment she is wearing or carrying isn't transformed.

fluffInfo.value: The Weeper is a carnivorous, living plant, a very dangerous foe, and it and the wood share an odd intimacy—when it awakens, so does the wood and many of the terrors growing in it, and some of those terrors act as its eyes and ears—and claws, and teeth. The Weeper emits a peculiar, maddening song throughout the wood, which *awakens* and draws any animal or beasts (and occasionally monsters) to it to feed or protect it. Some that try to resist the call are taken by madness.

*When it awakens, the Weeper cries out a maddening cacophony that is part song, part fluting pipes, part screams, and part sob. This sound echoes across the wood and continues until it sleeps once again or dies. The sound can be blocked in the usual ways, but any beast (and occasionally monster) that hears it spontaneously awakens and is drawn to it. Sometimes creatures become confused or enraged by the song, but more often than not, they simply move meekly to the Great Midden to be devoured. The thorny edges of the wood also awaken after a fashion—entwining to form a prickly outer wall. Trees and plants awaken across the wood, too, but they are slow to wake and not generally coordinated enough to attack. They typically simply try to trick outsiders into getting lost and dying.*
*The deadening nature of the wood makes tracing the source of the noise difficult, but clever PCs may seek to use this as a means of guiding themselves to The Weeper with an animal. Such animals move at the fastest pace they can but may themselves get lost or confused on the way. Any animal guide must succeed on a DC 7 Wisdom (*Survival*) check when it enters a hex for the first time or become lost. Lost animals move randomly into another hex but are always eventually drawn to the Weeper's song again.*
*Animal companions and familiars are not affected by this awakening but are aware of something odd in the air and likely show signs of nervousness as a result.*

traits.name: Alien Mind
traits.value: A creature who attempts to communicate with the weeper must succeed on a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or become frightened for 1 minute. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.value: The weeper has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The weeper makes three attacks, only one of which can be a Stinger attack.

actions.name: Stinger
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +4 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. *Hit:* 9 (**2d6 + 2**) piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or become poisoned for 1 minute. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

actions.name: Lashing Tendril
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +4 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. *Hit:* 7 (**2d4 + 2**) bludgeoning damage and the target is grappled (escape DC 12) if it is a Medium or smaller creature. The weeper has two lashing tendrils, each of which can grapple only one target.

actions.name: Grasping Tendril
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +4 to hit, reach 60 ft., one target. *Hit:* The target is grappled (escape DC 12), and the target must succeed on a DC 12 Strength saving throw or be pulled to up to 15 feet toward the weeper. It has two grasping tendrils, each of which can grapple only one target. If it is grappling at least one creature with its grasping tendril, the weeper can use this action to pull all creatures grappled in this way up to 30 feet closer to it.

bonusActions.name: Maddening Song (Recharge 4-6)
bonusActions.value: The weeper sings its maddening melody. The song doesn't typically affect sentient creatures but being subjected to it at close range can have deleterious effects. Each creature within 15 feet of the weeper that can hear its song must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or become poisoned until the end of its next turn, as the alien song muddles the mind and confuses the senses.

actions.name: Stinger
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +1 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. *Hit:* 1 piercing damage.

fluffInfo.value: *This twisted tree's face is made of cracked, black bark knotted into vaguely humanoid features, and thick tears of sap run down its face.*
Weeping treants clearly are related to other treants, but they are smaller than the normal variety. Their gnarled trunks are twisted, and their wood often groans when they move.

fluffInfo.name: Forest Wardens
fluffInfo.value: Weeping treants are protectors of dark, shadowy forests—particularly forests in the Plane of Shadow—and they are as long-lived as the trees themselves. They act as guardians for an entire forest or for something specific within the forest, and they have no pity for those carrying axes or fire.

fluffInfo.name: Skeptical Mein
fluffInfo.value: Weeping treants are terrifying and relentless when fighting in defense of their charge. They are inherently distrustful, particularly of anything not of the natural or shadow world, and they're notoriously difficult to fool or deceive.

fluffInfo.name: Enchanted Bitter Tears
fluffInfo.value: Sages and scholars debate why these creatures weep, but no one has come forward with a compelling reason beyond "it's what trees do." The weeping treants themselves refuse to speak on the matter. Their tears are occasionally components in druidic spells or items.

traits.name: Siege Monster
traits.value: The weeping treant deals double damage to objects and structures.

traits.name: Speak with Plants
traits.value: The weeping treant can communicate with plants as if they shared a language.

traits.name: Weep Acid
traits.value: Thick tears of dark, acidic sap stream continuously down the treant's face and trunk. A creature that touches the weeping treant or hits it with a melee attack while within 5 feet of it must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take 3 (**1d6**) acid damage.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The weeping treant makes two Slam or Rock attacks.

actions.name: Slam
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., single target. *Hit:* 15 (**3d6 + 5**) bludgeoning damage plus 3 (**2d6**) acid damage, and the target takes 3 (**1d6**) acid damage at the end of its next turn unless it or another creature takes an action to wipe off the acid.

actions.name: Rock
actions.value: *Ranged Weapon Attack:* +8 to hit, range 60/180 ft., one target. *Hit:* 21 (**3d10 + 5**) bludgeoning damage.

traits.name: False Appearance
traits.value: While the willow remains motionless, they are indistinguishable from a normal willow tree.

traits.name: Flammable
traits.value: If the willow takes fire damage, they catch fire and take 7 (**2d6**) fire damage at the start of each of their turns for 1 minute. The effect ends early if the willow takes cold damage or a creature uses an action to extinguish the flames.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The willow makes two Frenzied Branch attacks.

actions.name: Frenzied Branch
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +7 to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. *Hit:* 12 (**2d6 + 5**) bludgeoning damage. If the willow is on fire, this attack deals an extra 3 (**1d6**) fire damage.

actions.name: Tugging Roots
actions.value: Roots erupt from a point on the ground the willow can see within 60 feet of them. Each creature in a 10-foot sphere centered on that point must succeed on a DC 14 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone and moved up to 30 feet toward the willow, taking 4 (**1d8**) bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet moved.

actions.name: Willow's Tears
actions.value: The willow showers salty droplets on their bower. Each creature within 15 feet of the willow must succeed on a DC 14 Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by the willow (save ends at end of turn). While charmed in this way, a creature can't willingly move more than 15 feet away from the willow. If a creature charmed in this way takes damage, the effect ends for them.

traits.name: Alluring Cry
traits.value: The cry of the Weeping Willow attracts creatures in a 120-foot Emanation from the willow. At the start of each of its turns, a creature within the area must succeed on a DC 18 Charisma save or have the Charmed condition for 1 hour. On a success, the target is immune to this Weeping Willow's Alluring Cry for 24 hours.

While Charmed, the target also has the Incapacitated condition. On each of its turns, a Charmed creature must use its movement to approach the Weeping Willow by the most direct route, stopping when it is within 5 feet of the Weeping Willow. It doesn't avoid Opportunity Attacks, but if this movement would obviously cause damage (such as by walking through fire), the creature repeats the save before entering that space.

traits.name: Deep Rooted
traits.value: The Weeping Willow is immune to effects that would move it.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.value: The Weeping Willow has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The Weeping Willow makes two Slam attacks.

actions.name: Slam
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +8 to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. *Hit:* 25 (**4d10 + 3**) Bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Lignify
actions.value: *Constitution Saving Throw:* , one creature within 5 feet: DC 17. *Failure:* The target has the Restrained condition and repeats the save at the end of its next turn if it is still Restrained, ending the effect on itself on a success. *Failure:* The target has the Petrified condition instead of the Restrained condition, becoming a tree permanently. __Greater Restoration__ or similar magic returns an affected creature to their original form.

fluffInfo.value: *Serpent Lurking Beneath the Surface*

fluffInfo.name: Secret
fluffInfo.value: The sound of a hunting horn drives wellwyrms into a panicked frenzy.

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.value: The wellwyrm can breathe air and water.

traits.name: Hunting Terror
traits.value: If the wellwyrm hears a creature play a horn or similar Musical Instrument, it has the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The wellwyrm makes one Bite attack and uses Constrict.

actions.name: Bite
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +8, reach 10 ft. *Hit:* 15 (**2d10 + 4**) Piercing damage plus 21 (**6d6**) Poison damage.

actions.name: Constrict
actions.value: *Strength Saving Throw:* DC 16, one Medium or smaller creature the wellwyrm can see within 5 feet. *Failure:* 13 (**2d8 + 4**) Bludgeoning damage. The target has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14), and it has the Restrained condition until the grapple ends. The wellwyrm needn't spend extra movement to move during this grapple.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The priest makes two attacks, using Mace or Radiant Flame in any combination.

actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +5, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 6 (**1d6 + 3**) Bludgeoning damage plus 5 (**2d4**) Radiant damage.

actions.name: Radiant Flame

traits.name: Shapechanger
traits.value: The werebear ascetic can use its action to polymorph into a bear-humanoid hybrid or into its kindred bear form, or back into its true form, which is humanoid. Its statistics, unless noted, are the same in each form. Any armor it is wearing merges into its alternate forms. It reverts to its true form if it dies.

traits.name: Kindred Form
traits.value: The werebear's kindred form takes the shape of a Large bear. While in this form, it can speak to and understand bears, cannot take any actions requiring hands, adds its Constitution modifier to the result of any saving throw, and gains 25 temporary hit points the first time it takes this form each day.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The werebear makes three melee attacks, only one of which can be a bite.

actions.name: Bite (Hybrid or Kindred Form Only)
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. *Hit:* 16 (**3d8 + 3**) piercing damage. If the target is a humanoid, it must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or be cursed with werebear lycanthropy.

actions.name: Claw (Hybrid or Kindred Form Only)
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. *Hit:* 10 (**2d6 + 3**) slashing damage.

entries: **Speed**: *walk* 30 Ft., *walk* 40 Ft. (hybrid Form Only) or 50 Ft. (mammoth Form Only)

traits.name: Adapted
traits.value: The weremammoth can tolerate temperatures of 0 degrees Fahrenheit or lower without being subjected to the effects of extreme cold.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The weremammoth makes three attacks, using Spear or Trample in any combination. It can replace one attack with a Gore attack.

actions.name: Gore (Mammoth or Hybrid Form Only)
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +10, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 16 (**2d8 + 7**) Piercing damage. If the target is a Humanoid, it is subjected to the following effect. *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 12. *Failure:* The target is cursed. If the cursed target drops to 0 Hit Points, it instead becomes a Weremammoth under the GM's control and has 10 Hit Points. *Success* The target is immune to this weremammoth's curse for 24 hours.

actions.name: Spear (Humanoid or Hybrid Form Only)
actions.value: *Melee or Ranged Attack Roll:* +10, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. *Hit:* 17 (**3d6 + 7**) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Trample (Mammoth or Hybrid Form Only)
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +10, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 18 (**2d10 + 7**) Bludgeoning damage. If the target is a Large or smaller creature and the weremammoth moved 20+ feet straight toward it immediately before the hit, the target has the Prone condition.

bonusActions.name: Shape-Shift
bonusActions.value: The werewolf shape-shifts into a Large mammoth-humanoid hybrid or a Huge mammoth, or it returns to its true humanoid form. Its game statistics, other than its size, are the same in each form. Any equipment it is wearing or carrying isn't transformed.

entries: **AC**: 13 In Humanoid Form or 16 In Hybrid Form
**Immunities**: bludgeoning, piercing, slashing from nonmagical attacks that aren't silvered; charmed, frightened

traits.name: Grappler
traits.value: While a creature is grappled by the werewolf ravager, the werewolf has advantage on attack rolls against grappled targets, and the target takes an additional 3 **1d6** damage whenever it is hit with the werewolf's bite or claw attack.

traits.name: Shapechanger
traits.value: The werewolf can use its action to polymorph into a wolf-humanoid hybrid or back into its true form, which is humanoid. Any armor it is wearing merges into its hybrid form. It reverts to its true form if it dies.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The werewolf ravager makes two melee attacks. It can only make one bite attack per turn.

actions.name: Bite (Hybrid Form Only)
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. *Hit:* 12 (**2d8 + 3**) piercing damage. The target must succeed on a DC 14 Strength saving throw or be grappled.
Additionally, if the target is a humanoid, it must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or be cursed with werewolf lycanthropy.

actions.name: Claw (Hybrid Form Only)
