actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +5, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 6 (**1d6 + 3**) Bludgeoning damage plus 5 (**2d4**) Radiant damage.

actions.name: Radiant Flame
actions.value: *Ranged Attack Roll:* +5, range 60 ft. *Hit:* 11 (**2d10**) Radiant damage.

traits.name: Patriotic Outrider
traits.value: If the westwind rider has neither the Incapacitated or Frightened condition, friendly creatures within 30 feet that can see it gain Advantage on Wisdom and Charisma saving throws.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The westwind rider makes two Lance or Longsword attacks, in any combination.

actions.name: Lance
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +5 to hit, reach 10 ft. *Hit:* 8 (**1d10 + 3**) Piercing damage. If the westwind rider is mounted and directed its mount to move at least 10 feet straight toward a target immediately before the hit, the target takes an extra 11 (**2d10**) Piercing damage and, if it is Huge or smaller, it is pushed up to 10 feet away and has the Prone condition.

actions.name: Longsword
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +5, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 7 (**1d8 + 3**) Slashing damage or 8 (**1d10 + 3**) Slashing damage if used with two hands.

actions.name: Arcane Blast
actions.value: *Ranged Attack Roll:* +4, range 120 ft. *Hit:* 13 (**2d10 + 2**) Force damage.

fluffInfo.value: *The hairless canine scurries along the pier, dripping with water and carrying a fish in its jaws. Its finned claws click on the planks as a fishmonger yells from behind it.*

fluffInfo.name: Waterborne Packs
fluffInfo.value: Wharflings are hairless, aquatic canines with large, webbed feet and oversized mouths. Adept fish catchers, wharflings establish dens near the shores of oceans, lakes, and rivers, and they often move in family groups of three or more.

fluffInfo.name: Thieving Gits
fluffInfo.value: Those who have been bitten by a wharfling rightly fear their needle-like teeth, but most coastal communities hate the animal more for its propensity for theft. Their lairs are filled with stolen metal trinkets.

fluffInfo.name: Beach Swarms
fluffInfo.value: Periodically, wharflings congregate in huge numbers and tear along the shoreline for miles before returning to their dens. Why they gather this way is unknown, but most locals know to avoid the shore on these nights.

traits.name: Amphibious
traits.value: The wharfling can breathe air and water.

actions.name: Pilfering Bite
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 4 (**1d4 + 2**) piercing damage. Instead of dealing damage, the wharfling can steal one item the target is wearing or carrying, provided the item weighs no more than 10 pounds, isn't a weapon, and isn't wrapped around or firmly attached to the target, such as a shirt or armor.

fluffInfo.value: *This hulking primate looms over others of its kind. Its filthy white fur is matted and yellowed, and a deranged look haunts its blood-red eyes.*

fluffInfo.name: Awakened by Sorcery
fluffInfo.value: White apes were once docile, gentle giants that roamed forested hills and savannah lands. Two thousand years ago, a kingdom of mages awakened the apes and employed them as soldiers and servants, protecting and replacing the mages who were slowly dying of an unknown disease. When the mages died out, the apes remained.

fluffInfo.name: Arcane Wasting
fluffInfo.value: The enchantment that imbued the apes with intelligence also bleached their fur white and made them carriers of the arcane wasting disease that hastened their creators' demise. The apes are immune to the wasting's effects, but they can pass it to humanoids. Among spellcasters, the wasting spreads like a plague.

fluffInfo.name: Driven Away
fluffInfo.value: Their long relationship with the ancient mages built in the white apes a culture of communal knowledge and protection. This drives many white ape tribes to seek partnerships and companionship with nearby humanoid settlements. Unfortunately, their carrying of the arcane wasting disease leaves many humanoids terrified of them, viciously driving away the apes. They are acutely aware of the injustice that was done to them, and generations of exile have turned their desire for companionship to animosity, especially toward the spellcasters that are so susceptible to the disease they carry.

traits.name: Spellcasting Animosity
traits.value: If the white ape sees a creature cast a spell, the ape has advantage on attack rolls against that creature on the ape's next turn.

traits.name: Arcane Wasting
traits.value: Characterized by the slow mental deterioration it causes, arcane wasting is a disease that infects Humanoids and spreads through spellcasting. A creature infected with this disease manifests symptoms 1d4 days after infection, which include brain fog and difficulty recalling memories. Until the disease is cured, at the end of each long rest, the infected creature must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or its Intelligence and Wisdom scores are each reduced by 1d2. This reduction lasts until the creature finishes a long rest after the disease is cured. If the disease reduces a creature's Intelligence or Wisdom to 0, the creature dies. If the infected creature casts a spell on a Humanoid before the disease is cured, and the Humanoid is hit by the spell or fails the saving throw, that Humanoid must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or also become infected with the arcane wasting disease.

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.value: The white ape has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The white ape makes one Bite attack and two Fist attacks.

actions.name: Bite
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 13 (**2d8 + 4**) piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or contract the arcane wasting disease (see the Arcane Wasting trait).

actions.name: Fist
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +7 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 15 (**2d10 + 4**) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Frenzy (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: The white ape lashes out wildly at nearby creatures, flailing and biting. Each creature within 10 feet of the white ape must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, a creature takes 35 (**10d6**) bludgeoning damage and is pushed up to 10 feet away from the ape. On a success, a creature takes half the damage and isn't pushed. A creature that succeeds on this saving throw also has advantage on attack rolls against the white ape until the end of its next turn.

entries: **Immunities**: cold, necrotic, poison; charmed, exhaustion, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained, unconscious

traits.name: Blizzard Stalker
traits.value: Inclement weather (such as fog, snow or wind) doesn't impede the wraith's vision, and it has Advantage on Dexterity (*Stealth*) checks it makes in such conditions.

traits.name: Incorporeal Movement
traits.value: The wraith can move through other creatures and objects as if they were Difficult Terrain. It takes 5 (**1d10**) Force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

actions.name: Life Drain
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +6 (with Advantage during the first round of each combat), reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 16 (**3d8 + 3**) Necrotic damage plus 16 (**3d10**) Cold damage. If the target is a creature, its Hit Point maximum decreases by an amount equal to the Necrotic damage taken.

actions.name: Freezing Gale (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: *Constitution Saving Throw:* DC 14, each creature in a 30-foot Cone. *Failure:* 28 (**8d6**) Cold damage. *Success* Half damage.

actions.name: Create Walker (2/Day)
actions.value: The wraith targets a Humanoid corpse within 10 feet of itself that died from either Cold damage or exposure to extreme cold. The target's remains animate as either a Skeleton or a Zombie (depending on the state of the corpse, as determined by the GM) that has Immunity to Cold and Necrotic damage and shares the wraith's Blizzard Stalker trait. fluffInfo.value: The average Warg, a Wild Wolf is slightly larger than an ordinary wolf, and much more vicious. It can be encountered in a pack, but also as a solitary hunter or scout, ready to howl and alert other Wargs and evil creatures for miles around. Orcs learn how to ride upon Wild Wolves like men do on horses.

His attitude decreases one step to Hostile if they intentionally cause destruction or loot the town (such as looting the statue in area J2) but increases one step if they take action to help (such as putting out fires when the town is burning).

His attitude increases one step if the characters demonstrate selfless heroism or emotional tenderness. His attitude decreases one step if they are selfish or try to Influence him to learn a secret from him and fail their Charisma check.

fluffInfo.name: William's Secret

fluffInfo.value: *Howling wind encircles the dragon, filling and pushing its wings without the need for them to beat.*Wind dragons view anywhere touched by air as their property, and mortals point to them as the epitome of arrogance. Their narcissism is not without reason, for awe‑inspiring power supports their claims of rightful control. To the dragons of the shifting gales, strength is the ultimate arbiter.

fluffInfo.name: Braggarts and Bullies
fluffInfo.value: Wind dragons number among the greatest bullies and worst tyrants of mortal creatures. The sometimes-foolhardy creatures take offense at any perceived challenge and pleasure in humiliating rivals. They claim great swathes of territory but care little for its governance—they perceive mortals in that territory as possessions. Vassals receive only dubious protection in exchange for their loyalty. A wind dragon might seek bloody vengeance for the murder of a follower, but it's unlikely to go to any length to prevent the loss of that life in the first place.

fluffInfo.name: Lords of the Far Horizons
fluffInfo.value: Some believe that the dragons of the winds claim much more than they are capable of controlling or patrolling. Because they so love altitude, they prefer to rule and meet with earth-bound supplicants at the highest point available: the summit of a great mountain or atop a towering monument erected by fearful slaves. But these dragons are also driven by wanderlust and roam far from their thrones. They return eventually, ready to subjugate new generations and press a tyrannical claw on the neck of anyone who questions their right to rule.

fluffInfo.name: Perpetual Infighting
fluffInfo.value: These wandering tyrants are even more territorial among their own kind than they are among groundlings. Simple trespass by one wind dragon into the territory of another can lead to a battle to the death. Thus, their numbers never grow large, and the weakest among them are frequently culled.

fluffInfo.name: Portable Hoards
fluffInfo.value: Wind dragons' hoards typically consist of only a few truly valuable relics. Other dragons might sleep on a bed of coins, but common things bore wind dragons. While all true dragons desire and display great wealth, wind dragons concentrate their riches in a small number of notable trophies or unique historic items—often quite portable.

Unprotected flames, such as torches, in the area are extinguished, and protected flames, such as those in lanterns, have a 50 percent chance of being extinguished.

If a Winter Troll takes Fire damage, it immediately flees and attempts to find a safe place to recuperate.

fluffInfo.value: *A strange, mushroom-shaped creature leaps and flies through the air, spraying spores below itself.*

Wirbeln are spiral-shaped bipedal fungi that appear in an array of colors. Each individual is a specific hue that indicates the type of spores it produces. Wirbeln fungi cause minor coloration changes as a form of communication, depending on mood, temperament, or personality.

fluffInfo.name: Symbiotic Nomads
fluffInfo.value: The wirbeln fungi's origin is lost to history. Those familiar with the creatures know they are wanderers who roam until they find a suitable home, usually in deep and wild places. Home for the wirbeln fungi is best defined by the deep-rooted companionship they develop with other races, rather than a specific location. The wirbeln fungi form allegiances with numerous species, such as elves, gnomes, treants, and others.

fluffInfo.name: Fierce Protectors
fluffInfo.value: The main strength of wirbeln fungi is their ability to turn back adversaries threatening their gatherings. The extreme loyalty of the wirbeln reveals itself through a determination to defend its chosen community, even if such defense is detrimental to the individual wirbeln.

fluffInfo.name: Cunning Controllers
fluffInfo.value: Wirbeln fungi employ diversionary tactics, using their numbers and the natural terrain to their advantage to shirk capture and harass enemies. The wirbeln fungi continually fly out of reach, landing on high ledges or branches. They attack by shooting poisonous darts and dropping on enemies from above. They utilize body and mind-altering spores with overwhelming effects.

traits.name: Natural Appearance
traits.value: While the wirbeln remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from an ordinary fungus.

The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

All creatures that are not wirbeln fungi must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or take 5 (**1d10**) poison damage and be subject to one of the following effects for 1 minute, depending on the wirbeln's color: green is poisoned; red is blinded; yellow is incapacitated; blue is paralyzed; purple is frightened; and black is 5 (**2d4**) poison damage each round. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

fluffInfo.value: *This tiny ball of bright light seems to emanate from a crystalline center.*

*Some witchlights are willing to serve spellcasters as a familiar. Such witchlights have the following trait.*
***Familiar**: The witchlight can serve another creature as a familiar, forming a magic, telepathic bond with that willing companion. While the two are bonded, the companion can sense what the witchlight senses as long as they are within 1 mile of each other. While the witchlight is within 10 feet of its companion, the companion can't be blinded. At any time and for any reason, the witchlight can end its service as a familiar, ending the telepathic bond.*

fluffInfo.name: Wizard Servants
fluffInfo.value: Also called a "spooklight," a witchlight is a wizard's servant created from a tiny piece of quartz. It appears as a floating ball of flickering light similar to a will-o'-wisp. The hue of quartz used during the creature's creation determines the color of each witchlight's illumination. After the quartz is prepared, it is animated through an extended magical ritual cast under a full moon and a clear, starry sky. Consequently, they are extremely rare.

fluffInfo.name: Flashing Light Code
fluffInfo.value: A witchlight always shares the same alignment as its creator. Although it cannot speak, a witchlight understands the languages of its creator, and many spellcasters have taught their witchlights a coded cipher, allowing it to spell out words by flaring and dimming its light. When necessary, a witchlight can spell words in the air by flying so quickly that its trail of light forms letters.

fluffInfo.name: Free Roaming
fluffInfo.value: If the witchlight's master dies within one mile of the witchlight, it explodes in a brilliant but harmless flash of light. If it loses its master under any other circumstance, it becomes masterless. While masterless, it's free to do as it pleases. Evil masterless witchlights can be surprisingly cruel, not unlike will-o'-wisps. They seek to lure lost travelers into swamps or traps by using their glow to imitate the light of a safe haven. Conversely, good masterless witchlights guide travelers to places of safety or along safe paths, and they are prized by pilots and guides. Neutral witchlights exhibit a playful nature—sometimes mingling inside the cavities of weapons, gems, or other curiosities, causing them to be mistaken for magic items. More than one "wizard's staff " is just an impressive-looking stick with a witchlight perched on top.

fluffInfo.value: *Helper Made of Twine and Twigs (Ruby wrapped in a wicker cage)*

entries: **Immunities**: poison; deafened, exhaustion, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned

actions.name: Cursed Scratch
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +5, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 6 (**1d6 + 3**) Piercing damage plus 3 (**1d6**) Necrotic damage, and if the target is a creature, it has Disadvantage on attack rolls until the start of the witchwoven's next turn.

traits.name: Lethe
traits.value: When the wobalas's soul count is 0, they have advantage on attack rolls, disadvantage on saving throws, and their Intelligence score becomes 3 (-4). Additionally, the wobalas must use their movement on each of their turns to move as close as possible to the nearest creature they can sense with their soulsight, and then if they are able, they must use their action to attack and attempt to kill that creature. The wobalas can't act with any other purpose until they add 1 to their soul count.

traits.name: Soul Devourer
traits.value: When the wobalas reduces a creature who isn't a Construct or an Undead to 0 hit points or deals damage to a dying creature, the creature must make a DC 11 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the wobalas consumes the creature's soul and adds 1 to the wobalas's soul count. A creature whose soul is consumed in this way immediately dies, and they can't be restored to life by any means short of a __wish__ spell.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The wobalas makes three Despair Bolt attacks.

actions.name: Despair Bolt
actions.value: *Ranged Weapon Attack:* +10 to hit, range 150/600 ft., one creature. *Hit:* 16 (**3d6 + 6**) piercing damage plus 10 (**3d6**) psychic damage. The wobalas can burn 1 soul to make the target frightened of them for 1 minute. If the target is immune to being frightened, the wobalas regains the burned soul.

actions.name: Banishing Touch
actions.value: *Melee Spell Attack:* +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. *Hit:* 22 (**4d10**) psychic damage, and the target is teleported up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space the wobalas can see.

bonusActions.name: Flee, Mortal (Costs 1 Soul)

The target must succeed on a DC 16 Charisma saving throw or use their reaction, if available, to move their speed away from the wobalas by the most direct route possible, with no regard for their own safety. Creatures who can't be frightened succeed on this saving throw automatically.

fluffInfo.value: Like his totem, the wolf reaver dwarf travels in a pack with its brothers in arms, looking for worthy challenges to prove its combat prowess. Rushing into battle beside its allies for glory as much as plunder, the wolf reaver dwarf throws caution to the wind and fights without care for its own safety.

traits.name: Danger Sense
traits.value: While conscious, the wolf reaver dwarf has advantage on Dexterity saving throws.

traits.name: Dwarven Resilience
traits.value: The wolf reaver dwarf has advantage on saving throws against poison.

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.value: The wolf reaver dwarf has advantage on attack rolls against a creature if at least one of the dwarf's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn't incapacitated.

traits.name: Reckless
traits.value: At the start of its turn, the wolf reaver dwarf can gain advantage on all melee weapon attack rolls during that turn, but attack rolls against it have advantage until the start of its next turn.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The wolf reaver dwarf makes one Battleaxe attack and two Spear attacks, or it makes three Handaxe attacks.

actions.name: Battleaxe
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +6 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target. *Hit:* 8 (**1d8 + 4**) slashing damage, or 9 (**1d10 + 4**) slashing damage if used with two hands.

actions.name: Handaxe
actions.value: *Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack:* +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. *Hit:* 7 (**1d6 + 4**) slashing damage.

actions.name: Spear
actions.value: *Melee or Ranged Weapon Attack:* +6 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft., one target. *Hit:* 7 (**1d6 + 4**) piercing damage, or 8 (**1d8 + 4**) piercing damage if used with two hands to make a melee attack.

fluffInfo.value: Greater in stature, cruelty and cunning than ordinary Wargs, a Wolf-chieftain is called upon by its lesser kin to deal with serious threats, like bands of travelling adventurers trespassing into Warg territory. A Wolf-chieftain is never encountered alone, but always surrounded by a pack of Wild Wolves.

traits.name: Fear of Fire
traits.value: If a Wolf-chieftain takes fire or radiant damage, it must succeed on a Charisma (*Intimidation*) check (DC 10 + damage taken) or be frightened until the end of its next turn.

traits.name: Keen Hearing and Smell
traits.value: The Wolf-chieftain has advantage on Wisdom (*Perception*) checks that rely on hearing or smell.

traits.name: Pack Tactics
traits.value: The Wolf-chieftain has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of the Wolf-chieftain's allies is within 5 feet of the creature and the ally isn't incapacitated.

actions.name: Bite
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 10 (**2d6 + 3**) piercing damage. If the target is a creature, it must make a DC 13 Strength saving throw or be knocked prone.

fluffInfo.value: *Facsimile Grown of Root and Vine*

fluffInfo.name: Secret
fluffInfo.value: Woodwarped possess a deep fear of axes—tools capable of severing not only their bodies but their bond to the forest. The mere sight of an axe is enough to hold the creatures at bay, and the bite of its blade slices them like smoke.

traits.name: Aversion to Axes
traits.value: At the start of the woodwarped's turn, if it can see a creature holding a Battleaxe, a Greataxe, or a Handaxe, it has the Frightened condition until the start of its next turn.

traits.name: Thorns
traits.value: At the start of each of its turns, the woodwarped deals 5 (**2d4**) Piercing damage to any creature it is grappling or any creature grappling it.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The woodwarped makes two Claw attacks.

actions.name: Claw
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +6, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 7 (**1d6 + 4**) Slashing damage plus 4 (**1d8**) Poison damage. If the target is a Medium or smaller creature, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC 14) from one of two claws.

actions.name: Thorn Spray (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: *Dexterity Saving Throw:* DC 13, each creature in a 15-foot Emanation originating from the woodwarped, with Disadvantage if Grappled by it. *Failure:* 14 (**4d6**) Piercing damage, and the target has the Poisoned condition. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. After 1 minute, it succeeds automatically. *Success* Half damage only.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The skald makes two Shortword or two Shortbow attacks.

actions.name: Shortsword
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 10 (**2d6 + 3**) Piercing damage.

actions.name: Shortbow
actions.value: *Ranged Attack Roll:* +6 to hit, range 80/320 feet., one target. *Hit:* 10 (**2d6 + 3**) Piercing damage.

bonusActions.name: Heroic Oration (Recharge 5-6)
bonusActions.value: One creature of the skald's choice within 30 feet of it that can hear it has Advantage on attack rolls and ability checks until the start of the skald's next turn.

entries: **HP**: 7 + seven times caregiver's level (number of d8 Hit Dice equal to their caregiver's level)

traits.name: Move as One
traits.value: While the worg's caregiver is mounted on the worg, opportunity attacks against the worg or their caregiver are made with disadvantage. The worg's caregiver can mount or dismount the worg by spending 5 feet of movement.

actions.name: Signature Attack (Bite)
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +3 plus PB to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* **1d6 plus PB** piercing damage.

actions.name: 1st Level: Overwhelming Attack (2 Ferocity)
actions.value: The worg makes a signature attack. On a hit, the attack deals an extra **PB** damage, and the target can't take reactions until the start of the worg's next turn.

actions.name: 3rd Level: Brutal Charge (5 Ferocity)
actions.value: The worg moves up to their speed without provoking opportunity attacks. During or at the end of this move, they can make a signature attack against one target.

actions.name: 5th Level: Bite Rampage (8 Ferocity)
actions.value: The worg makes signature attacks against PB creatures of their choice within 5 feet of them. On a hit, a target is knocked prone.

fluffInfo.value: *Robes cover the rotting flesh and lifeless gray hair of this humanoid. Fine, arm-length worms wriggle through abscesses in its flesh and its empty eye-sockets, and it moves with a stooped, shuffling gait.*
Wormhearted suffragans are devoted followers of Qorgeth, Demon Lord of Worms, who they believe is the servant and forerunner of a dark goddess of worms and decay.

fluffInfo.name: Dark Worm Hearts
fluffInfo.value: Formerly, the suffragans were priests or holy officers of other faiths, but their hearts were corrupted by their fear and loathing. Once pledged to the service of the devouring worm, Qorgeth replaced their hearts with a bulbous, writhing conglomeration of worms, which permits them to carry on with an undead mockery of life.

fluffInfo.name: Prey on the Wounded
fluffInfo.value: Suffragans frequently follow armies, visiting battlefields shortly after the fighting is over. In the guise of gravediggers, nurses, or chirurgeons, they select their targets from among the dead and dying for as long as they can remain undetected, spreading their worms to create new servants for their demon lord.

fluffInfo.name: Fear Light and Radiance
fluffInfo.value: Wormhearted suffragans are especially susceptible to the flesh-searing power of light. For this reason, they avoid priests of the sun god or gods of light. At night, however, they are a walking contagion, infesting enemies with parasitic worms that devour victims from within.

entries: **Languages**: the languages it knew in life

traits.name: Magic Resistance
traits.value: The wormhearted suffragan has advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

traits.name: Master of Undeath
traits.value: A Humanoid killed by the wormhearted suffragan's disease rises 1d4 hours later as a skeleton or zombie (the suffragan's choice), unless the Humanoid is restored to life or its body is destroyed. Between its disease and its Animating Worms, the suffragan can have no more than fifteen total skeletons and zombies under its control at one time.

traits.name: Undead Nature
traits.value: The wormhearted suffragan doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The wormhearted suffragan makes two Worm-Coated Fist or Paralyzing Bolt attacks.

actions.name: Worm-Coated Fist
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +6 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 10 (**2d6 + 3**) bludgeoning damage plus 7 (**2d6**) necrotic damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or contract a disease. Until the disease is cured, the target can't regain hp, and its hp maximum decreases by 7 (2d6) every 24 hours. This reduction lasts until the target finishes a long rest after the disease is cured. The target dies if this effect reduces its hp maximum to 0.

actions.name: Paralyzing Bolt
actions.value: *Ranged Spell Attack:* +6 to hit, range 60 ft., one target. *Hit:* 17 (**4d6 + 3**) necrotic damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or be paralyzed until the end of its next turn.

actions.name: Animating Worms (3/Day)
actions.value: The wormhearted suffragan touches the body of a dead Humanoid, passing on some of the suffragan's worms. The worms fill the target, animating it as a skeleton or zombie (the suffragan's choice) under the suffragan's control.

fluffInfo.value: *Parasitical Physician*

fluffInfo.name: Secret
fluffInfo.value: Wormhost surgeons are drawn to seek out and infest sapient victims, so intelligent creatures with veiled minds slip beneath the surgeons' notice.

traits.name: Regeneration
traits.value: The surgeon regains 10 Hit Points at the start of each of its turns. If it takes Poison damage, this trait doesn't function at the start of its next turn. The surgeon dies only if it starts its turn with 0 Hit Points and doesn't regenerate.

traits.name: Veiled Ignorance
traits.value: A creature whose mind can't be read, or that is under the effect of a __Mind Blank__ or __Nondetection__ spell, has the Invisible condition toward the surgeon (this ignores the surgeon's Blindsight).

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The surgeon makes two Bone Saw attacks.

actions.name: Bone Saw
actions.value: *Melee Attack Roll:* +7, reach 5 ft. *Hit:* 7 (**1d6 + 4**) Slashing damage plus 4 (**1d8**) Psychic damage.
Critical *Hit:* If the target is a creature, its Intelligence score decreases by 1d4. The target dies if this reduces that score to 0.

actions.name: Infested Spray (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: The surgeon unleashes a spray of worm-ridden cerebral fluid. *Dexterity Saving Throw:* DC 14, each creature in a 20-foot Cone. *Failure:* 17 (**5d6**) Psychic damage, and the target is infested with larval parasitic worms. The target takes 7 (**2d6**) Psychic damage at the end of each of its turns as the worms burrow toward its brain. The ongoing damage ends when the target takes Poison damage or is targeted by an effect that ends the Poisoned condition. *Success* Half damage only. *Failure or Success*: If the target is reduced to 0 Hit Points by this Psychic damage, the worms reach its brain and it dies. A Humanoid slain in this way rises 24 hours later as a wormhost surgeon.

fluffInfo.name: Vengeful Restoration
fluffInfo.value: Wraithroot trees are the product of foul necromancy and transmutation rituals that first see a tree awakened, gifting it with advanced intelligence and imbuing its roots with mobility. But the __awakened tree's__ first moments of joyous awareness are tragically cut short as necromantic energy courses through it, channeling rage and evil to transform it into a wraithroot—filled with longing to obliterate the life it so fleetingly enjoyed.

fluffInfo.name: Wraithroot Sites
fluffInfo.value: In Tal'Dorei, wraithroots can be found in a number of locations, including the Parchwood Timberlands below Whitestone, the Torian Forest along the southwestern edge of the Cliffkeep Mountains, the Grey Valley north of Kraghammer, and the Moldered Grove southeast of the Ashkeeper Peaks.

fluffInfo.name: Alignment
fluffInfo.value: Neutral evil.

traits.name: False Appearance
traits.value: While the wraithroot tree remains motionless, it is indistinguishable from a normal tree.

traits.name: Wraith Shift
traits.value: On its turn, the wraithroot tree can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. The tree does not provoke opportunity attacks while moving, and must finish its movement in a space unoccupied by any Large or larger objects or creatures. Any Medium or smaller creature in the tree's space when it finishes moving is pushed to the nearest unoccupied space of the creature's choice. Medium or smaller objects in the tree's space are pushed to the nearest unoccupied spaces of the tree's choice.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The wraithroot tree makes two slam attacks.

actions.name: Slam

actions.name: Rock
actions.value: *Ranged Weapon Attack:* +11 to hit, range 60/180 ft., one target. *Hit:* 28 (**4d10 + 6**) bludgeoning damage.

actions.name: Wraithstorm (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: The wraithroot tree pulls life energy from the area around it, leaving creatures temporarily frail. Each creature that is not a construct or undead within 30 feet of the tree must succeed on a DC 16 Constitution saving throws or have its speed halved and gain vulnerability to bludgeoning damage until the end of the tree's next turn.

actions.name: Grasping Strike

actions.name: Punch Down

fluffInfo.value: Magic is beyond the means of most commonfolk in the continent. Few can afford the services of the Amethyst Academy, and priests of the Sacred Flame and Old Gods alike are selective with their divine magic, offering their boons to devout worshippers or those in dire need only. However, apothecaries are seldom so selective, especially those who operate in remote regions or clandestinely within large cities.

fluffInfo.name: Desperate Vanity
fluffInfo.value: Lesser nobles and vain merchants occasionally seek out apothecaries not for a cure to an ailment, injury, or sickness, but in the hopes of augmenting some quality of themselves they find deficient. These individuals may come to an apothecary looking for a miraculous means to become taller or more comely, reverse aging, or even gain supernatural or magical abilities.

fluffInfo.name: Medical Malpractice
fluffInfo.value: Unfortunately for their patients, unscrupulous apothecaries may be perfectly willing to offer an experimental method or untested procedure in exchange for an affordable price, seeking an opportunity to trial their latest concoction upon a hapless yet willing subject. When these ill-conceived techniques inevitably go awry, the subjects find themselves transformed into a grotesque mockery of themselves.

fluffInfo.name: Promised Cure
fluffInfo.value: The transformation leaves the patient half-mad. Some are manipulated in the hopes of being cured one day, or tricked into believing that they must remain in the care of their "doctor" until they have "recovered" from the procedure. Many lash out in rage, fleeing into the wilderness, back alleys, or hidden away in their homes. Those unable to return to their former lives in fear or shame may remain, however.

fluffInfo.name: Useful Lackeys
fluffInfo.value: Left without the means to restore their former appearance, these wretched patients accept roles as orderlies, guards, and assistants to the apothecary responsible for their tormented contention. Truly psychotic apothecaries may increase their control over their patients through invasive brain surgery, chemical conditioning, and forced indoctrination. These terrible procedures render these unfortunate individuals fiercely loyal to the apothecary, imbuing them with a fanatical drive to protect them even at the cost of their own lives.

fluffInfo.name: The Varied Victims of Many Malpractices
fluffInfo.value: Wretched Patients represent the unfortunate victims of apothecaries' experiments. No matter their area of study, the deranged minds of evil scientists know no bounds with their experimentation on willing subjects in the name of occult science.

fluffInfo.name: Alienist
fluffInfo.value: Often those with mental instability or muddled minds turn to an Alienist. These patients are rendered into mindless and obedient servants through mind control, mental conditioning, and mind-altering procedures. Alienists have been known to go as far as remove portions of their victims' brains or remove their brains entirely while keeping the subject alive.

fluffInfo.name: Chemist
fluffInfo.value: Those looking for tinctures and tonics to ease all manner of ailments have turned to Chemists, often unaware of the danger of their compounds. These patients are often subject to new experimental procedures that leave them burned, or scarred, disfigured by chemical research. In some cases, the chemical procedures can leave the victims hairless, blind, or cause their skin to muddle and scar over completely.

fluffInfo.name: Exorcist
fluffInfo.value: An Exorcists patients seek help with possessions that may or may not be real. These haunted people can find themselves at the hands of mad scientist and spiritualist who will use the willing patient to summon or trap demonic forces. Sometimes these patients are simply what remains after a demonic or spiritual possession, where after the removal, the victim is left numb and catatonic, having lost most of themselves to the entity that inhabited them. More sinister exorcists will perform this procedure on purpose, placing powerful entities into a patient, only to remove it and render the patient hollow and willing to become a subject to the apothecary.

fluffInfo.name: Mutagenist
fluffInfo.value: The failed experiments of a Mutagenist can leave all manner of strange disfigurations and abnormalities upon their patients. Everything from unusual growths, cankers, and tumors, to fully growing extra limbs, eyes, mouths, and other such strange occurrences. These patients become hideous mockeries of their former selves and over time, become reliant on the doctor to keep their growths and mutations in check.

fluffInfo.name: Pathogenist
fluffInfo.value: When sick with disease, or dealing with unknown poisons, subjects will go to a Pathogenist. Those who take their practices too far often use subjects as vessels for experimentation. Subjects are often riddled with diseases, sores, boils, at times losing their teeth and fingernails to unnatural decay, their skin turning shades of yellow, green, or purple. They appear sickly, carrying a many pathogens, toxins, and diseases.

fluffInfo.name: Reanimator
fluffInfo.value: Reanimators are sought out when a patient has lost a limb, or had severe injury that would leave them scarred or disfigured. The Reanimators who take their practice too far will use the subject as a means of experimentation. Attaching new limbs to them, testing the lengths they can go by adding multiple limbs, or a second head, additional fingers or toes, subjects over time can become a patchwork of various parts that have been removed, reattached, or swapped.

fluffInfo.name: Study the Foe
fluffInfo.value: Characters proficient in *Medicine* gain Advantage on Wisdom (*Insight*) or Intelligence (*Investigation*) checks to study a Wretched Patient, learning the following based on the result:

fluffInfo.name: (10+) Broken by Experimentation
fluffInfo.value: You know the creature's Conditioned Obedience trait.

fluffInfo.name: (15+) Fervent Loyalty
fluffInfo.value: You know these creatures protect their creator via their Protective Impulse Reaction.

fluffInfo.name: Combat Tactics
fluffInfo.value: Wretched Patients are simple minions. They defend themselves and reluctantly fight at the command of their creator. If their creator dies, Wretched Patients flee or cower.

fluffInfo.name: Animus:
fluffInfo.value: Aberration.

fluffInfo.name: Fluid:
fluffInfo.value: Monster Blood, Contaminated Ichor.

fluffInfo.name: Organs:
fluffInfo.value: Eyes, Heart, Brain, Guts.

fluffInfo.name: Bones:
fluffInfo.value: Skull, Spine.

fluffInfo.name: Natural Weapons:
fluffInfo.value: Blades.

fluffInfo.name: Hair:
fluffInfo.value: Stitches, Hair.

fluffInfo.name: Hide:
fluffInfo.value: Skin.

fluffInfo.value: *This small metallic globe skitters about on many-jointed legs.*

fluffInfo.name: Cleaning Constructs
fluffInfo.value: Created by gnomish tinkerers, xanka are constructs whose purpose is cleaning up their masters' messy workshops. Most xanka are built from copper, brass, or bronze, but gold, silver, and platinum varieties have been seen in the houses of nobles and rich merchants. Xanka are not built for fighting—their instinct tells them to skitter for cover when danger threatens—but they defend themselves when cornered.

fluffInfo.name: Follow Commands
fluffInfo.value: These constructs understand and obey simple commands that relate to the removal of garbage. They can communicate with each other through whirs, clicks, and flashing lights, but those who have studied this communication find it is rarely more than a relaying of commands from the master between xanka to more efficiently carry out the master's wishes.

fluffInfo.name: Absorb Matter
fluffInfo.value: When a xanka touches material to its globular body, it absorbs that material into itself, quickly breaking the material down into magical energy. They can use this energy to power themselves for further tasks or to protect themselves from danger by expelling the energy in a burst. Tinkerers use xanka to keep their homes and cities clear of refuse.

entries: **Immunities**: poison, psychic; charmed, exhaustion, frightened, paralyzed, petrified, poisoned
**Languages**: understands the languages of its creator but can't speak

traits.name: Absorb
traits.value: Any nonmagical object that touches the xanka's central globe, any nonmagical weapon that hits the xanka, or any nonmagical object, structure, or creature hit by the xanka's Dismantling Leg attack begins to deteriorate. If it is a structure or an object that isn't being worn or carried, up to a 1-foot cube of the structure or object is destroyed.

If it is an object worn or carried by a creature, the creature must succeed on a DC 11 Dexterity saving throw to avoid the item being affected by the xanka's Absorb. If the object is a weapon, the weapon takes a permanent and cumulative -1 penalty to damage rolls. If the weapon's penalty drops to -5, the weapon is destroyed. If the object is armor or a shield, the armor or shield takes a permanent and cumulative -1 penalty to the AC it offers. Armor reduced to an AC of 10 or a shield that drops to a +0 bonus is destroyed. If the target is a creature, the creature must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution saving throw or take 2 (**1d4**) necrotic damage.

traits.name: Construct Nature
traits.value: The xanka doesn't require air, food, drink, or sleep.

actions.name: Dismantling Leg
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 6 (**1d8 + 2**) bludgeoning damage, and the target is subjected to the xanka's Absorb trait.

actions.name: Release Energy (Recharge 5-6)
actions.value: The xanka releases energy created from absorbed material in a burst. Each creature within 10 feet of it must make a DC 11 Dexterity saving throw, taking 7 (**2d6**) force damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

fluffInfo.value: *As the ichor drips away and the smoke clears, you see a monstrous creature standing 15 feet tall, a canine, fanged head with two jagged horns protruding from its crown.*

traits.name: Demonic Restoration

traits.name: Magic Resistance

actions.name: Pummel
actions.value: *Dexterity Saving Throw:* DC 17, one creature Grappled by Xarashtar. *Failure:* 15 (**3d6 + 5**) Bludgeoning damage. *Success* Half damage.

fluffInfo.value: *Watching with many rows of eyes, this mantis creature strikes with slashing claws and recurved barbs dripping with venom.*

fluffInfo.name: Dimensional Travelers
fluffInfo.value: The clandestine xhkarsh are beings from another cosmic cycle. Their devices and armor are incomprehensible—possibly even incompatible with—creatures of this reality.

fluffInfo.name: Tamper with Fate
fluffInfo.value: The xhkarsh utilize their fate-altering powers to distort personal histories and manipulate mortal destinies like puppeteers. By doing this, they realign the universe toward their own, esoteric ends—but what those ends might be, only the xhkarsh know.

fluffInfo.name: Foes of Skein Witches
fluffInfo.value: Skein witches and valkyries are perpetual enemies of the xhkarsh, whom they accuse of perverting the proper run of destiny for both great heroes and ordinary folk.

entries: **Languages**: Common, Deep Speech, telepathy 60 ft., Undercommon

traits.name: Corruption's Bond
traits.value: The xhkarsh ignores the range restriction on its telepathy when communicating with a creature whose fate it has corrupted. In addition, it can pinpoint the location of any such creature, as well as sense the creature's general state of health. These effects function even if the xhkarsh and the creature are on different planes of existence.

traits.name: Interdimensional Nature
traits.value: The xhkarsh doesn't require air, food, drink, sleep, or ambient pressure.

actions.name: Multiattack
actions.value: The xhkarsh makes two Claw attacks and one Fate-Altering Stinger attack.

actions.name: Claw
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. *Hit:* 13 (**2d8 + 4**) slashing damage plus 9 (**2d8**) poison damage.

actions.name: Fate-Altering Stinger
actions.value: *Melee Weapon Attack:* +8 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. *Hit:* 15 (**2d10 + 4**) piercing damage, and the target must succeed on a DC 16 Charisma saving throw or have its fate corrupted. A creature with corrupted fate has disadvantage on Charisma checks and Charisma saving throws, can't be targeted by any divination magic, can't be perceived through magical scrying sensors, and is immune to any effect that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts. The target's fate can be restored, ending the corruption and breaking the xhkarsh's magical tie to the target, by a __dispel evil and good__ spell or similar magic.

actions.name: Invisibility
actions.value: The xhkarsh magically turns invisible until it attacks or uses Seize Strand, or until its *concentration* ends (as if *concentrating* on a spell). Any equipment the xhkarsh wears or carries is invisible with it.

actions.name: Seize Strand
actions.value: One creature whose fate is corrupted by this xhkarsh must succeed on a DC 16 Charisma saving throw or be affected by the __geas__ spell for 8 hours. While under the geas, the affected creature must perform a specific, seemingly minor task that furthers the decades-long goals of the xhkarsh. Such a task could be writing a letter to a specific person, damaging a seemingly random piece of equipment, or speaking a specific sentence to a particular person. The xhkarsh can use Seize Strand on a particular creature no more than once every 24 hours, regardless of success or failure on the saving throw.

On a failed save, a creature takes 71 (**11d12**) lightning damage and can't take reactions until the end of their next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and suffers no other effect.

bonusActions.name: Gone in a Flash
bonusActions.value: Xogomoc teleports, along with any creatures inside him (see Into the Storm), up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space he can see. Each creature within 10 feet of the space he left must make a DC 25 Constitution saving throw, taking 22 (**4d10**) thunder damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

traits.value: Eight eyes float around Xorannox and create his Eye Psionics. If Xorannox fails a saving throw, he can destroy a random floating eye (chosen by rolling a d8) and succeed instead. If an eye is destroyed, a new eye pops of out of Xorannox's face to replace it 24 hours later.

actions.name: Eye Psionics
actions.value: Xorannox creates three of the following psionic eye effects. Unless otherwise stated, each eye targets a creature who he can see within 120 feet of him. He can't use the same effect twice on a turn.

entries: **1. Charm Beam**: The targeted creature must succeed on a DC 17 Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by Xorannox for 1 hour, or until he harms the creature or one of their allies.

**2. Compulsion Beam**: The targeted creature must succeed on a DC 17 Intelligence saving throw or use their reaction, if available, to move up to their speed toward the closest ally they can see and make one weapon attack against them. Creatures who can't be charmed are unaffected.

**3. Memory Beam**: The targeted creature must make a DC 17 Intelligence saving throw. On a failed save, if the creature has unexpended spell slots, they expend a spell slot of their highest remaining level, with no effect. If they don't have unexpended spell slots, they instead lose proficiency with a weapon they're holding or carrying for 1 minute (save ends at end of turn).

**4. Toxic Vapors**: Xorannox chooses a point he can see within 120 feet of him. Each creature within 10 feet of the point must succeed on a DC 17 Constitution saving throw or be poisoned for 1 minute (save ends at end of turn).

**5. Telekinetic Field**: Xorannox chooses a point he can see within 120 feet of him. Each enemy within 10 feet of the point must succeed on a DC 17 Strength saving throw or be moved up to 30 feet in any direction and take 7 (**2d6**) force damage at the end of the move. Additionally, Xorannox can target any object within 10 feet of the point that weighs 300 pounds or less and isn't being worn or carried, moving it up to 30 feet in any direction. Xorannox can also exert fine control on objects with this effect, such as manipulating a simple tool or opening a door or a container.

**6. Lightning Bolt**: Xorannox shoots a 5-foot-wide, 60-foot-long line of lightning. Each creature in the line must succeed on a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw, taking 36 (**8d8**) lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

**7. Explosion**: Xorannox chooses a point he can see within 120 feet of him. Each creature within 10 feet of the point must make a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw, taking 36 (**8d8**) fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

**8. Necrosis Beam**: The targeted creature must succeed on a DC 17 Constitution saving throw or immediately take 55 (**10d10**) necrotic damage and lose 7 (**2d6**) hit points at the start of each of their turns. If this effect reduces a target's hit points to 0, they die. The effect ends if Xorannox dies or can't see the target. This psionic effect can't be used again while this effect persists.

fluffInfo.value: *The massive oxen shakes its head, sending a flock of birds flying. It groans out a yawn that sets nearby trees rattling.*

Ychen bannogs are massive, ox-like beasts with thick, wooly coats and great horns like the gods' battering rams. They stand over forty feet tall at the shoulder and weigh hundreds of tons. Despite their awe-inspiring size, these towering creatures are peaceful wanderers in the wilderness, where their calls echo for miles.

fluffInfo.name: Strongest Beasts in the World
fluffInfo.value: Legends are built on the sturdy backs of ychen bannog. They are the strongest beasts of burden in the known world. Tamed ychen bannogs can haul entire communities, or even small castles, and a clever dwarf with a ychen bannog at its disposal can carve out enormous riverbeds, haul enormous stones, or reshape entire valleys with ease.

fluffInfo.name: Ychen Warships
fluffInfo.value: Giants have a particular affinity with the ychen bannogs. In times of war, giants sometimes build complex siege platforms atop these beasts, making effective transport for small armies of giants. Thankfully, ychen bannogs are rare enough that even seeing one in an army is a tale to be told for generations.

fluffInfo.name: Louder Than Thunder
fluffInfo.value: When riled, an ychen bannog can bellow loudly enough to shatter stones and knock down walls.

traits.name: Siege Monster
traits.value: The ychen bannog deals double damage to objects and structures.
